functions.name: basis_def2tzvp_prims_flat
functions.what: (exponent, coefficient), one primitive per row.

functions.name: basis_def2tzvp
functions.what: The def2-TZVP basis set as a `Basis` record.

functions.name: basis_def2tzvp_nao
functions.what: The Cartesian and spherical AO counts of one atom of each element, `1` to `18`, as the generator counted them.

functions.name: basis_key
functions.what: PySCF's key for a basis name: lower case, no `-`, `_` or spaces.

functions.name: basis_module
functions.what: The module of lib/basis whose table PySCF's key `k` names, or "" when no table here has that name.

functions.name: basis_named
functions.what: The basis set PySCF names `name`, from the tables of lib/basis the program uses.

functions.name: bas_ncart
functions.what: Cartesian components in a shell of angular momentum `l`.

functions.name: bas_nsph
functions.what: Spherical components in a shell of angular momentum `l`.

functions.name: bas_odfact
functions.what: The odd double factorial `(2k-1)!!`, with `(-1)!! = 1`.

functions.name: bas_powers
functions.what: The powers of every Cartesian component of a shell, `[ncart, 3]`, in PySCF's order.

functions.name: bas_fc
functions.what: The factor between PySCF's Cartesian component and the unit one: PySCF = unit * F. It is one for s and p [test "F squared matches PySCF's int1e_ovlp_cart diagonal for xx and xy"].

functions.name: bas_nc
functions.what: The component factor `Nc`: it cancels the double factorials of the Gaussian moments, so `cn` can be shared by every component of a shell.

functions.name: bas_nr
functions.what: The radial norm `Nr(a, l) = (2a/pi)^(3/4) (4a)^(l/2)`.

functions.name: bas_prim_overlap
functions.what: Overlap of two unit primitives of one shell with exponents `a` and `b`.

functions.name: shell_atom
functions.what: The atom shell `s` sits on.

functions.name: shell_l
functions.what: The angular momentum of shell `s`.

functions.name: shell_cart0
functions.what: The index of shell `s`'s first Cartesian basis function.

functions.name: shell_sph0
functions.what: The index of shell `s`'s first spherical basis function.

functions.name: shell_nprim
functions.what: The number of primitives of shell `s`.

functions.name: shell_p0
functions.what: The row of shell `s`'s first primitive in the primitives table.

functions.name: shell_f0
functions.what: The index of shell `s`'s first basis function: spherical when `sph = 1`, Cartesian otherwise.

functions.name: bas_atom_pos
functions.what: The position of atom `a`, `[x, y, z]` in bohr.

functions.name: bas_prim_exp
functions.what: The exponent of primitive `p`.

functions.name: bas_nao_cart
functions.what: Cartesian AO count of a shell pack.

functions.name: bas_nao_sph
functions.what: Spherical AO count of a shell pack.

functions.name: bas_ao_table
functions.what: One row per Cartesian AO: (shell, atom, lx, ly, lz), `[nao_cart, 5]`. Rows follow the shells in order and the components in PySCF's order, which is what `SH_CART0` counts.

functions.name: bas_contract
functions.what: Contracted coefficients `cn[nprimtot]` in the unit-Cartesian convention: raw coefficient times `Nr(a_p, l)`, with the shell rescaled to contracted self-overlap one [test "16 seeded shells up to f come out with unit self-overlap in every component"].

functions.name: bas_rng
functions.what: Test helper: the next uniform number in `(0, 1)` from a Park-Miller state held in `st[0]`, so a failing shell can be quoted by its seed.

functions.name: bas_moment_self_overlap
functions.what: Test helper: the self-overlap of component `(lx, ly, lz)` of shell `s`, summed from 1-D Gaussian moments, one axis at a time. It shares no formula with `bas_prim_overlap`.

functions.name: bas_random_shells
functions.what: Test helper: `nsh` random shells with `l < BAS_T_NL` (s to f), from one to `BAS_T_NPRIM_MAX` primitives each, exponents spread from $10^{-1.5}$ to $10^{3.5}$ and coefficients that are sometimes negative. Returns the shells and prims packs.

functions.name: molecule_bohr
functions.what: The molecule of atomic numbers `z[natm]` at `xyz[natm, 3]` (bohr), with every atom's shells from basis `b`: neutral, spin from the electron count's parity, spherical functions.

functions.name: molecule_from
functions.what: The molecule of atomic numbers `z[natm]` at `xyz[natm, 3]` in angstrom, with every atom's shells from basis `b`.

functions.name: molecule_packs
functions.what: A molecule from packs made elsewhere: neutral, spin from the parity, spherical functions.

functions.name: mol_nelectron
functions.what: The number of electrons.

functions.name: mol_nalpha
functions.what: Alpha electrons: `(N + spin) / 2`.

functions.name: mol_nbeta
functions.what: Beta electrons: `(N - spin) / 2`.

functions.name: mol_enuc
functions.what: The repulsion between the nuclei, `sum over pairs Z_A Z_B / R_AB`. A ghost atom (`Z = 0`) adds nothing, as in PySCF.

functions.name: mol_lmax
functions.what: The highest angular momentum of the basis.

functions.name: mol_spherical
functions.what: `1` when the run uses spherical functions that differ from the Cartesian ones: `cart` is `0` and some shell has `l >= 2`. Up to p the two sets are the same functions in the same order, so nothing is transformed.

functions.name: mol_nao
functions.what: The number of basis functions the SCF sees.

functions.name: mol_coverage
functions.what: The elements a basis set has functions for, as "H to Ar" when they run without a gap from the first, else listed.

functions.name: mol_is_bohr
functions.what: Whether `unit` names bohr rather than angstrom, as PySCF reads `unit=`: a unit starting with B or AU is bohr, one starting with A is angstrom, and any other unit stops the run.

functions.name: molecule_in
functions.what: The molecule of `atoms` (text: `symbol x y z` per atom, `;` or newlines between atoms, or an XYZ file) with coordinates in `unit`, in the basis set PySCF names `basis`.

functions.name: molecule
functions.what: The molecule of `atoms` (angstrom, as PySCF's default) in the basis set PySCF names `basis`: `molecule("O 0 0 0; H 0 -0.757 0.587; H 0 0.757 0.587", "6-31g")`.

functions.name: boys_series_one
functions.what: `F_n(x)` at one order from its series. The terms grow while `2x > 2n + 2k + 3` and shrink after, so the stop test only fires past the peak, and a fixed term count would be wrong at the top of the range.

functions.name: boys_switch
functions.what: The switch `x_n` for order `n`: at or above it `boys_asym_up` is exact to rounding in every order up to `n`. The list is checked, value by value, against mpmath by `tools/boys_reference.py` (see the header for the rule).

functions.name: boys_down
functions.what: `F_0 .. F_nmax` from `F_nmax = top`, by the downward step.

functions.name: boys_series_down
functions.what: Every order from `0` to `nmax`: the series at `nmax`, then downward.

functions.name: boys_asym_up
functions.what: `F_0 = sqrt(pi/x)/2` and upward with the `e^-x` term kept, at or above `boys_switch(nmax)`; the series below it.

functions.name: boys_values
functions.what: The production entry: whichever member is most accurate at this `x`.

functions.name: boys_gl_nodes
functions.what: Gauss-Legendre nodes and weights on `[-1, 1]`: `GL[0, i]` is a node and `GL[1, i]` its weight. Newton's method on `P_m` from the usual cosine guess; it converges quadratically, so a fixed `BOYS_GL_NEWTON_IT` steps is past the point where the nodes stop moving.

functions.name: boys_gl_pass
functions.what: All orders at once on `npan` equal panels: one `exp` per node, then the powers `t^(2n)` by repeated multiplication.

functions.name: boys_quadrature
functions.what: Gauss-Legendre with the panel count doubled until every order agrees with the previous pass to `BOYS_QUAD_TOL` relative. At large `x` the integrand is a spike of width about `1/sqrt(x)` next to `t = 0` (for `n = 0`) or near `sqrt(n/x)`, which one panel cannot resolve; halving the panels resolves it within a few passes, and Gauss-Legendre converges fast once it is resolved, so the pass that meets the stop is at least as accurate as the stop [test "the series, the quadrature and the Taylor step each match mpmath to 1e-13"]. A stop at the size of the rounding noise between passes never fires: the doubling runs to `BOYS_QUAD_MAXPAN` panels, and the rounding of the long sum grows past the stop.

functions.name: boys_grid_range
functions.what: A Taylor grid for orders up to `ncap`, holding `npts` nodes from node index `i0` (node `i` sits at `x = i h`). Row `0` is a header `[h, i0, npts, ncap]`; row `r >= 1` holds `F_0 .. F_(ncap+K)` at node `i0 + r - 1`, the `K` extra orders being what the Taylor step needs.

functions.name: boys_grid_new
functions.what: The grid a caller builds once, for orders up to `nmax` and arguments up to `xmax`. It stops at the switch, because above it `boys_grid_eval` uses the asymptotic form, which is exact there and needs no table. The switch is taken at the highest order and over all orders below; the generator checks that `boys_switch` never falls with `n`, so that is the largest one.

functions.name: boys_grid_eval
functions.what: `F_0 .. F_nmax` at `x` from grid `G`. With `d = x - x0` for the nearest node `x0`, `F_nmax(x) = sum_k F_(nmax+k)(x0) (-d)^k / k!`, since `dF_n/dx = -F_(n+1)`. `|d| <= 0.05` and `F_(n+k) <= F_n`, so stopping at `k = 8` leaves at most `0.05^9 / 9! = 5.4e-18` of `F_nmax`. The lower orders then come downward. An `x` outside the grid, or an order above the one it was built for, falls back to the series, so a short grid is slow rather than wrong.

functions.name: boys_taylor
functions.what: The Taylor grid as a registry member: a one-node grid at the node nearest `x`, built on the spot. Slow, since it runs the series anyway, but it is the same evaluation code the per-caller grid uses.

functions.name: boys_methods
functions.what: The registry, production member first. Every member takes `(nmax, x)` and returns `F[0..nmax]`. Both parameters are numbers, as the frozen stage signature `(nmax, x) -> Arr` has them, and every member annotates them `: Num` and its result `-> Arr`, so the kinds are fixed in the member itself and not inferred from whichever call a program happens to make.

functions.name: herm_nh
functions.what: Hermite functions with `t + u + v <= L`.

functions.name: herm_tuv
functions.what: The Hermite index list for total order `L`, `[nh, 3]`: `t` counts up, then `u`, then `v`. Every table in this family uses this order.

functions.name: herm_esize
functions.what: Entries of a flat E table for one axis with powers up to `la` and `lb`.

functions.name: herm_efill
functions.what: Fill the flat 1-D table `E(i, j, t)`, `i <= la`, `j <= lb`, `t <= i + j`, into `E` from entry `e0` on, at `e0 + (i (lb + 1) + j) (la + lb + 1) + t`. `X` is `A - B` on this axis. The table is overwritten, so a caller can reuse one buffer for every primitive pair.

functions.name: herm_etab
functions.what: The frozen form: `E[la+1, lb+1, la+lb+1]` for exponents `a`, `b` and `XAB = A - B` on one axis.

functions.name: herm_rfill
functions.what: Fill `S[0 .. (L+1)^3)` with `pref * R(0; t, u, v)` at offset `(t (L+1) + u) (L+1) + v`, for `t + u + v <= L`. `S` needs `2 (L+1)^3` entries: the upper half is the scratch cube for odd `n`. `F` holds `F_0 .. F_L` at `alpha (X^2 + Y^2 + Z^2)`. Entries with `t + u + v > L` are left as they were, and nothing reads them.

functions.name: herm_rfill_box
functions.what: `pref * R(0; t, u, v)` for `t <= Tx`, `u <= Ty`, `v <= Tz` only, into `S` at `s0 + (t (Ty+1) + u) (Tz+1) + v`, using `2 (Tx+1)(Ty+1)(Tz+1)` entries from `s0` on. `F` holds `F_0 .. F_(Tx+Ty+Tz)`. This is what one integral needs: `(xx, xx | xx, xx)` has `Ty = Tz = 0`, so it builds one line of entries per level, where the full cube of the same order builds every entry with `t + u + v <= L`.

functions.name: herm_rtab
functions.what: The frozen form: `R[L+1, L+1, L+1]` with `R[t, u, v] = R(0; t, u, v)` for exponent `p`, `PC = P - C` and Boys values `F[0 .. L]` at `p |PC|^2`. Entries with `t + u + v > L` are zero.

functions.name: herm_grid
functions.what: A Boys grid for `herm_boys_fill`: `boys_grid_new(nmax, xmax)` with the switch of every order `n <= nmax` copied into its header row at column `BOYS_GRID_HDR + n` (the row is at least `nmax + 9` wide and `boys_grid_eval` reads only its first `BOYS_GRID_HDR` columns). `boys_switch` builds its list on every call, and an integral loop calls the fill once per primitive quartet.

functions.name: herm_boys_fill
functions.what: `F_0 .. F_nmax` at `x` into `F`, from a grid `G` built once by the caller with `herm_grid`. It is `boys_grid_eval` without the allocations: an integral loop calls it once per primitive quartet, and a fresh array each time would cost more than the Taylor step. Above the switch it is the asymptotic form with upward recursion, and an `x` or order the grid does not cover falls back to the series, exactly as in `lib/hf/boys`.

functions.name: herm_lambda
functions.what: Test helper: the Hermite Gaussian `d^t/dP^t exp(-p (x - P)^2)` at `x`, from the Hermite polynomial recursion. It shares no code with `herm_efill`.

functions.name: herm_overlap_1d
functions.what: Test helper: the 1-D overlap `int x_A^i x_B^j exp(-a x_A^2 - b x_B^2) dx` from the binomial expansion about `P` and the Gaussian moments. Another route to `E(i, j, 0) sqrt(pi/p)`.

functions.name: md1_grid
functions.what: The Boys grid a one-electron build needs: orders up to `2 lmax`.

functions.name: md1_pair
functions.what: S, T and V for shell pair `(sa, sb)`, as `[3, ncart_a * ncart_b]` with the component pair `(ia, ib)` at column `ia * ncart_b + ib`. `cn` comes from `bas_contract` and `G` from `md1_grid`.

functions.name: md1_all
functions.what: S, T and V for the whole basis, `[3, n, n]` over Cartesian AOs. Each shell pair is computed once, for `sa >= sb`, and mirrored, so every matrix is exactly symmetric.

functions.name: md1_scatter
functions.what: Write a `md1_pair` block into `M` at both `(sa, sb)` and `(sb, sa)`.

functions.name: md1_pick
functions.what: One matrix out of `md1_all`.

functions.name: md1_s
functions.what: Integral-stage members `(atoms, shells, prims) -> [n, n]`.

functions.name: md1_h
functions.what: The core Hamiltonian `T + V`.

functions.name: md1_gap
functions.what: Test helper: the largest absolute gap between matrix `k` of `M` and `R`.

functions.name: es_pair
functions.what: Index of the pair (i, j), in either order.

functions.name: es_npair
functions.what: Pairs of `n` orbitals.

functions.name: es_index8
functions.what: Packed-8 index of (ij|kl), for any of its eight index orders.

functions.name: es_len8
functions.what: Length of the packed-8 vector for `n` orbitals.

functions.name: es_get
functions.what: (ij|kl) read from the packed vector.

functions.name: es_pack8
functions.what: Pack a dense, 8-fold-symmetric `[n, n, n, n]` tensor. Only entries with i >= j, k >= l and ij >= kl are read.

functions.name: es_unpack8
functions.what: The dense `[n, n, n, n]` view of a packed vector. Meant for small `n`: the view holds $n^4$ doubles.

functions.name: es_rng
functions.what: One Park-Miller step on the state in `st[0]`; returns the new weight in $(0, 1)$. The state must start in `1 .. ES_MINSTD_M - 1`.

functions.name: es_checksums
functions.what: `[sum Gp^2, sum w_k Gp_k]`, summed in index order, with w_k the k-th Park-Miller weight from `seed`. The seeded sum catches errors that a sum of squares misses, such as two values swapped.

functions.name: es_sample_index
functions.what: `m` packed indices drawn with the same generator: floor(w_k * len). Indices can repeat.

functions.name: es_sample_gap
functions.what: The largest abs(Gp[idx[k]] - vals[k]) over the samples.

functions.name: es_sym_tensor
functions.what: Test helper: a dense tensor that is 8-fold symmetric bit for bit. Addition and multiplication of two doubles commute exactly, so building every entry from commutative pieces of (i, j) and of (k, l) makes all eight orders equal without relying on the packing code under test.

functions.name: es_sym_defect
functions.what: Test helper: the largest disagreement among the eight orders of any entry.

functions.name: mderi_packsize
functions.what: Entries of one pack for groups of `ca` and `cb` shells of angular momentum `la` and `lb` with `npp` primitive pairs: a 5-number header `[la, lb, npp, nab, nh]`, `(p, Px, Py, Pz)` per primitive pair, then `E_ab` as `[nab, npp * nh]`, `nab = ca cb ncart(la) ncart(lb)` rows.

functions.name: mderi_fillpack
functions.what: Fill the pack for the group pair of `nga` shells from `sa` and `ngb` from `sb` at `ST[off ..]`. `cn` is from `bas_contract`. The shells of a group share their primitives' exponents, so the primitive pairs, their centers and the Hermite expansions are the first shells'; each row of `E_ab` carries one shell pair's contraction coefficients, rows ordered `((a nb_grp + b) ncart_a + i) ncart_b + j` for shell `a` of the first group, `b` of the second, components `i` and `j`.

functions.name: mderi_store_groups
functions.what: The store for the group pairs in `PL` (`[npl, 2]`, rows `(ga, gb)`) of the groups `GT` (`[ng, 2]`, rows `(first shell, shells)`), as one flat array: `ST[0]` = pair count, `ST[1]` = largest l, then the directory (`MDERI_DIR_LEN` entries a pair), then the packs.

functions.name: mderi_store_pairs
functions.what: The store for the shell pairs in `PL` (`[npl, 2]`, rows `(sa, sb)`), each shell a group of its own.

functions.name: mderi_seg_groups
functions.what: Every shell a group of its own, `[nsh, 2]`: the segmented store.

functions.name: mderi_same_prims
functions.what: `1` when shells `s` and `t` are on the same atom, have the same angular momentum and the same primitive exponents: the contractions of one general contraction, which the basis tables list as segmented shells one after the other.

functions.name: mderi_groups
functions.what: The shell groups, `[ng, 2]` rows `(first shell, shells)`: runs of consecutive shells with the same atom, angular momentum and exponents. A group's primitive integrals are computed once for all its shells.

functions.name: mderi_canon_pairs
functions.what: Every canonical pair `a >= b` of `nsh` shells (or groups), numbered `a (a + 1)/2 + b`.

functions.name: mderi_store
functions.what: The store over every canonical pair of shell groups (`mderi_groups`): the production one.

functions.name: mderi_store_seg
functions.what: The store over every canonical shell pair, each shell its own group: the segmented store, which checks the grouped one.

functions.name: mderi_grid
functions.what: The Boys grid an ERI build needs: orders up to `4 lmax`.

functions.name: mderi_emat
functions.what: `E_ab` of the pack at `o`, copied out as a matrix for `@`.

functions.name: mderi_hoff
functions.what: Offsets `(t D + u) D + v` into an R cube of side `D`, for the Hermite list of order `L`; with `signed = 1`, the sign `(-1)^(t+u+v)` instead.

functions.name: mderi_block
functions.what: The block `(ab|cd)` for bra pair `k1` and ket pair `k2` of the store, as `[ncart_a * ncart_b, ncart_c * ncart_d]`. `G` is from `mderi_grid`.

functions.name: mderi_schwarz
functions.what: `Q[k] = sqrt(max (ab|ab))` over the components of store pair `k`.

functions.name: mderi_qlist
functions.what: The flat quartet list `[nq, 2]` of `(bra pair, ket pair)` rows with `bra >= ket`, keeping a row when `Q[bra] Q[ket] >= tol`. A negative `tol` keeps every row, and `Q` is then not read.

functions.name: mderi_put
functions.what: Write block `B` of store pairs `(k1, k2)` into the packed vector. Only the canonical entries (`i >= j`, `k >= l`, and `ij >= kl` when the two pairs are the same) are written, so every slot is written once.

functions.name: mderi_put_at
functions.what: `mderi_put` with the functions numbered by the shells-table columns `c0col` (first function) and `ncol` (how many): `SH_CART0` and `SH_NCART` for a Cartesian block, `SH_SPH0` and `SH_NSPH` for a spherical one. The shells are in the same order in both numberings, so the same canonical quartets hold every canonical integral of either. A row of the block is `((a nb_grp + b) n_a + i) n_b + j` (lib/hf/md_eri's pack rows), and within one group pair only `i >= j` (by function number) is written.

functions.name: mderi_do
functions.what: One row of the quartet list, computed and written; a def of its own so that its arrays are freed on return, on whichever thread ran it.

functions.name: mderi_build
functions.what: Packed-8 ERIs over Cartesian AOs, skipping quartets with `Q_AB Q_CD < tol` (a negative `tol` skips nothing and never computes `Q`), over the grouped store.

functions.name: mderi_build_st
functions.what: `mderi_build` over a given store: grouped or segmented.

functions.name: mderi_screened
functions.what: Integral-stage members `(atoms, shells, prims) -> packed-8`.

functions.name: mderi_tstore
functions.what: The pair transforms of the store's group pairs as one flat array. `TS[k]` is where pair k's matrix starts, `[rows of its block, nsph_a nsph_b times the shell pairs]`, block diagonal with one `M_a (x) M_b` per shell pair, followed by its transpose; `TS[k]` is `-1` when both groups are up to p, whose block of `M` is the identity. `M` is the c2s matrix of lib/hf/cart2sph.

functions.name: mderi_tmat
functions.what: The `[rows, cols]` matrix stored at `TS[o ..]`, copied out for `@`.

functions.name: mderi_block_sph
functions.what: The block `(ab|cd)` of store pairs `k1`, `k2` over spherical functions: the Cartesian block of `mderi_block` with the bra pair's transform transposed on the left and the ket pair's on the right (`mderi_tstore`), a side skipped when its transform is the identity.

functions.name: mderi_sph_do
functions.what: One row of the quartet list over spherical functions, computed, transformed and written; a def of its own so its arrays are freed on return.

functions.name: mderi_sph_build
functions.what: Packed-8 ERIs over spherical functions, `M` the c2s matrix: each quartet moved to spherical functions as it is computed, so no Cartesian packed vector is built and none is read back. Schwarz screening as in `mderi_build` (a negative `tol` skips nothing).

functions.name: mderi_sph
functions.what: The production ERIs over spherical functions: Schwarz-screened at `MDERI_SCREEN_TOL`, transformed block by block. `mderi_screened` followed by `tr4_blocks` (lib/hf/transform) is the same thing in two passes and checks it.

functions.name: mderi_quartet
functions.what: `(ab|cd)` for four shells in any order, `[na nb, nc nd]`: the entry point for single quartets and for tests.

functions.name: mderi_prim1_size
functions.what: Scratch entries `mderi_prim1` needs for components up to `lmax`.

functions.name: mderi_erow
functions.what: Where `E(la, lb, 0)` sits in a table `herm_efill` wrote at `e0` for powers `la`, `lb`.

functions.name: mderi_prim1
functions.what: One integral `(ab|cd)` over four unit-normalized primitive components. `PQ` is `[4, 7]`, a row `(exponent, x, y, z, lx, ly, lz)` per function; `G` is from `herm_grid` with order at least the total `l`; `W` is scratch of `mderi_prim1_size(lmax)` entries and `F` of `4 lmax + 1`. It builds only the E entries of these powers and only the R entries inside their box (`herm_rfill_box`), so one value costs far less than the shell block that holds it. It is the path for spot checks on bases too big for a full build, and it shares no matrix code with `mderi_block`.

functions.name: mderi_schwarz_excess
functions.what: Test helper: the largest `|(ij|kl)| / sqrt((ij|ij)(kl|kl)) - 1` over every packed entry; the Schwarz bound holds when it is at most rounding.

functions.name: mderi_diag_gap
functions.what: Test helper: the largest gap between the pair diagonal `(ij|ij)` of `Gp` and a reference list of it.

functions.name: mderi_ref_gaps
functions.what: Test helper: the largest of the relative checksum gaps and the sample and diagonal gaps of `Gp` against one reference set.

functions.name: scf_defaults
functions.what: The production options: every registry at its production member, DIIS over `OPT_DIIS_N_DEFAULT` matrices from the second iteration on (the guess's Fock matrix stays out, as in PySCF), at most `OPT_MAXIT_DEFAULT` iterations, converged at an energy change below `OPT_ETOL_DEFAULT` and a commutator below `OPT_GTOL_DEFAULT`, each integral stage by its production member.

functions.name: scf_checked
functions.what: The defaults with every integral stage cross-checked: all members run and must agree.

functions.name: opt_array
functions.what: The column array of options `o` for `na` alpha and `nb` beta electrons and nuclear repulsion `enuc`. `OPT_PRODUCTION` is `1` when `o.cross_check` is `0`.

functions.name: opt_new
functions.what: The column array of the defaults, with no electrons: what a registry member's own tests pass it.

functions.name: mdjk_put
functions.what: Add block `B` of store pairs `(k1, k2)` into the J and K copies of one chunk, `W[w0 + 2d]` (J) and `W[w0 + 2d + 1]` (K) for each density `d`. Rows and columns of `B` are numbered as lib/hf/md_eri's packs number them, a shell pair of the two groups at a time.

functions.name: mdjk_one
functions.what: One quartet of the list into chunk `c`'s copies; a def of its own so the block is freed as soon as it has been added.

functions.name: mdjk_chunk
functions.what: Chunk `c` of `nch`: quartets `c, c + nch, c + 2 nch, ...` of the list, added into `W`, the chunk's own copies of J and K.

functions.name: mdjk_direct_nch
functions.what: J and K with the quartets dealt into `nch` chunks. The result does not depend on the thread count; it depends on `nch` only through the order of the final sums.

functions.name: mdjk_direct
functions.what: The J/K registry member: `X1 .. X3` = atoms, shells, prims; `D` is `[ndens, n, n]`; the result is `[2 ndens, n, n]`, J then K per density.

functions.name: mdjk_dmax
functions.what: The largest `|D|` over the functions of each pair of shell groups (`GT`, lib/hf/md_eri's `mderi_groups`) and every density, `[ng, ng]`, symmetric. A group's functions are consecutive.

functions.name: mdjk_pair
functions.what: One quartet computed and added into `W`; a def of its own so the block is freed as soon as it has been added.

functions.name: mdjk_chunk_screened
functions.what: Chunk `c` of `nch` of the screened build: bra pairs `c, c + nch, ...`, each against every ket pair up to it, a quartet kept when it passes the Schwarz test (`Q_AB Q_CD >= tol_s`) and the density test (header), with `Dm` over the store's shell groups.

functions.name: mdjk_screened_q
functions.what: J and K of `D` with Schwarz and density screening, from the Schwarz factors `Q` of the store's pairs (`mderi_schwarz`); `[2 ndens, n, n]`.

functions.name: mdjk_direct_screened
functions.what: The density-screened J/K registry member: `X1 .. X3` = atoms, shells, prims. It computes the Schwarz factors itself; the SCF's direct member (lib/hf/jk_direct) takes them from the basis blob instead.

functions.name: mdjk_rand_dens
functions.what: Test helper: `nd` seeded symmetric densities `[nd, n, n]` with entries in (-1, 1), from the Park-Miller generator of `lib/hf/eri_store`.

functions.name: mdjk_dense_gap
functions.what: Test helper: J and K of `D` by dense contraction of the packed vector, as two `[n^2, n^2]` matrix-vector products: `J = Gj @ vec(D)` with `Gj[(i,j),(k,l)] = (ij|kl)`, and `K = Gk @ vec(D)` with `Gk[(i,j),(k,l)] = (ik|jl)`. The largest gap to `JK` over every entry is returned.

functions.name: mdg_rfill
functions.what: `herm_rfill` for `L <= MDG_RMAX` by the def of its class; `-1` and nothing written above it (no `stop`, so that a `parallel for` may call it).

functions.name: mdg_pair

functions.name: mdg_gather
functions.what: The gather of a ket pair of total order `L2 <= 2 MDG_LMAX` by the def of its order; `-1` and nothing written above it.

functions.name: mdg_t2
functions.what: The pair transform `(M_a (x) M_b)^T`, `[nsph_a nsph_b, ncart_a ncart_b]`, from the c2s blocks of shells `sa` and `sb` in the block-diagonal `M`.

functions.name: mdg_pair_general
functions.what: `mdg_pair` for a class with no generated kernel: the same entries from `herm_etab` (lib/hf/hermite) in loops, into the flat `V`.

functions.name: mdg_fillpack
functions.what: The E matrix of the group pair of `nga` shells from `sa` and `ngb` from `sb`; its primitive pairs' `(p, Px, Py, Pz)` into `ST` at `off` (md_eri's pack header and primitive list) and its row index at `ix`. With `sph = 1` the rows are spherical, `T` the pair transform; else Cartesian and `T` is not read.

functions.name: mdg_nrows
functions.what: The rows of pair `k` of the store: shells in the two groups times functions per shell pair.

functions.name: mdg_pick
functions.what: Entry `i` of `A` followed by `B`.

functions.name: mdg_packs
functions.what: The E matrices of store pairs `k0 .. k0 + n - 1`, filling their packs in `ST` as it goes. Built by halves: a loop that appended every pair's record would keep all the arrays made so far, and the C runtime checks each array it frees at the end of an iteration against those it keeps (`viv_arena_release_kept`), which made the loop quadratic in the pairs (study/ports/pyscf/FRICTION.json, pyscf-024).

functions.name: mdg_store
functions.what: The store over every canonical pair of md_eri's shell groups: md_eri's directory and pack headers in `ST` (no E entries) followed by the pairs' row indices, and each pair's E matrix in `EM`. `M` is the c2s matrix when `sph = 1`.

functions.name: mdg_htab
functions.what: md_eri's `mderi_hoff` for every case a build with shells up to `lmax` meets, made once, as one flat table with rows of `herm_nh(2 lmax)`. With `nl = 4 lmax + 1` totals and `lp = 2 lmax + 1` pair orders, row `Ls nl + L` holds the cube offsets `(t D + u) D + v`, `D = L + 1`, of the Hermite list of order `Ls`, and row `lp nl + Ls` the signs `(-1)^(t+u+v)`.

functions.name: mdg_put
functions.what: Write block `B` of store pairs `(k1, k2)` into the packed vector, the canonical entries only, as md_eri's `mderi_put_at` does, through the pairs' row indices in `ST`.

functions.name: mdg_block
functions.what: The block `(ab|cd)` for bra pair `k1` and ket pair `k2`, `[rows of k1, rows of k2]`, in the store's functions (spherical or Cartesian). `G` is from `mderi_grid`, `HT` from `mdg_htab`. md_eri's `mderi_block` with the generated R kernel, the kept E matrices and the offset tables made once.

functions.name: mdg_gather_general
functions.what: The general gather of one primitive quartet's Hermite values: `BR[o + hc ncol + ha] = sign(hc) S[offset(hc) + offset(ha)]`, the offsets and signs read from `mdg_htab`'s table (`ia`, `ic` and `isg` where the bra offsets, the ket offsets and the ket signs start). The generated `mdg_gather` does the same with the ket offsets as constants; this def runs the orders above it and checks it (the test below).

functions.name: mdg_schwarz
functions.what: `Q[k] = sqrt(max (ab|ab))` over the rows of store pair `k`.

functions.name: mdg_schwarz_one
functions.what: `Q[k]` for one store pair; a def of its own so its block is freed on return.

functions.name: mdg_do
functions.what: One row of the quartet list, computed and written; a def of its own so its arrays are freed on return.

functions.name: mdg_build
functions.what: Packed-8 ERIs, Schwarz-screened at `tol` (a negative `tol` skips nothing), over spherical functions when `sph = 1` (`M` the c2s matrix) and Cartesian ones otherwise.

functions.name: mdg_sph
functions.what: The production ERIs over spherical functions, `M` the c2s matrix of lib/hf/cart2sph: Schwarz-screened at `MDERI_SCREEN_TOL`.

functions.name: mdg_screened
functions.what: The production ERIs over unit-normalized Cartesian functions, Schwarz-screened at `MDERI_SCREEN_TOL`: the integral-stage member `(atoms, shells, prims) -> packed-8`.

functions.name: mdg_jk_put
functions.what: Add block `B` of store pairs `(k1, k2)` into the J and K copies `W[w0 + 2d]` (J) and `W[w0 + 2d + 1]` (K) of each density `d`: md_direct's `mdjk_put` through the rows' function indices in `ST`.

functions.name: mdg_dmax
functions.what: md_direct's `mdjk_dmax` over spherical functions when `sph = 1` and Cartesian ones otherwise: the largest `|D|` over the functions of each pair of shell groups, `[ng, ng]`.

functions.name: mdg_jk_pair
functions.what: One quartet computed and added into `W`; a def of its own so the block is freed as soon as it has been added.

functions.name: mdg_jk_chunk
functions.what: Chunk `c` of `nch`: md_direct's `mdjk_chunk_screened` on this module's quartets. Bra pairs `c, c + nch, ...`, each against every ket pair up to it, a quartet kept when it passes the Schwarz test (`Q_AB Q_CD >= tol_s`) and the density test.

functions.name: mdg_schwarz_basis
functions.what: The Schwarz factors of the store `mdg_jk_screened` builds, over spherical functions when `sph = 1` (`M` the c2s matrix): a property of the basis, computed once per SCF (lib/hf/jk_direct's blob).

functions.name: mdg_jk_screened
functions.what: J and K of the densities `D[nd, n, n]` in the run's functions (spherical when `sph = 1`, `M` the c2s matrix; Cartesian otherwise), Schwarz and density screened, from the Schwarz factors `Q` of `mdg_schwarz_basis`; `[2 nd, n, n]`, J then K per density.

functions.name: c2s_binom
functions.what: n choose k, exact in doubles for the small arguments used here.

functions.name: c2s_unit_gram
functions.what: The overlap of the unit Cartesian components of one shell, `[ncart, ncart]`, when they share one radial part. Per axis the Gaussian moment gives `(p + q - 1)!!` for powers p and q with p + q even, and 0 when it is odd; the unit factors `Nc` scale the result so the diagonal is 1.

functions.name: c2s_cart_row
functions.what: The row of component (lx, ly, lz) in PySCF's Cartesian order: the components with a larger lx come first, and within one lx a larger ly.

functions.name: c2s_closed
functions.what: M_l by hand for l <= 3. Rows are the unit Cartesian components in PySCF's order, columns the spherical functions in PySCF's order. Each entry is a coefficient of the polynomial named above it times sqrt((2lx-1)!! (2ly-1)!! (2lz-1)!!), divided by the polynomial's norm. Above l = 3 it returns `c2s_general(l)`.

functions.name: c2s_sph_col
functions.what: The column of the spherical function with index m in PySCF's order. For p PySCF keeps x, y, z, which are m = 1, -1, 0.

functions.name: c2s_general
functions.what: M_l for any l from the real solid harmonic expansion  S_lm ~ sum_t sum_u sum_w (-1)^(t + (w - wm)/2) 4^-t C(l,t) C(l-t,|m|+t) C(t,u) C(|m|,w) x^(2t + |m| - 2u - w) y^(2u + w) z^(l - 2t - |m|)  with t = 0 .. (l - |m|)/2, u = 0 .. t, and w running over the integers up to |m| that are even for m >= 0 and odd for m < 0 (wm is 0 or 1 to match). This is Helgaker's sum with v = w/2. The overall constant is left out: each column is scaled afterwards to unit norm in the metric of `c2s_unit_gram`, which also converts monomial coefficients to unit ones.

functions.name: c2s_block
functions.what: The production M_l: the hand-written table where it exists, the general construction above it.

functions.name: c2s_basis
functions.what: The block-diagonal M for a basis, `[nao_cart, nao_sph]`: shell s puts its M_l at rows SH_CART0 and columns SH_SPH0, and everything between shells is zero. Then PySCF's spherical X is `M^T X_unit M`.

functions.name: c2s_orth_gap
functions.what: The largest entry of abs(M^T G M - I) for one block.

functions.name: tr2_dense
functions.what: `M^T X M` as two full matrix products, `[nao_sph, nao_sph]`. The shells pack is used only for the two sizes.

functions.name: tr2_blocks
functions.what: `M^T X M` one shell pair at a time: the (a, b) spherical block is `M_a^T X_ab M_b`, where `M_a` is shell a's diagonal block of M. Every pair is done, so X need not be symmetric.

functions.name: tr2_back_dense
functions.what: `M D M^T`, `[nao_cart, nao_cart]`: a spherical density as the Cartesian one with the same contractions, since Tr(D M^T X M) = Tr((M D M^T) X).

functions.name: tr2_back_blocks
functions.what: `M D M^T` one shell pair at a time.

functions.name: tr4_dense
functions.what: The dense four-index transform of a dense `[nc, nc, nc, nc]` tensor, one index per pass: l, then k, then j, then i. Returns `[ns, ns, ns, ns]`.

functions.name: tr4_quarter
functions.what: Packed Cartesian ERIs to packed spherical ones through the dense view and four quarter transformations. Meant for n <= 30, like `es_unpack8`.

functions.name: tr4_quartet
functions.what: The spherical block `[ma, mb, mc, md]` of shells (a, b, c, d), from the Cartesian block read out of the packed vector and the four `M_l` blocks. Any order of the four shells works, because `es_index8` accepts any order. A shell up to p is the same in both sets, so its pass is skipped.

functions.name: tr4_blocks
functions.what: Packed Cartesian ERIs to packed spherical ones, one canonical shell quartet at a time: a >= b, c >= d and pair(a, b) >= pair(c, d). Every canonical spherical (pq|rs) lies in one of those quartets, since the symmetry that maps a function quartet to its canonical order maps its shell quartet the same way.

functions.name: tr4_two_pass
functions.what: The ERIs over spherical functions in two passes: every Cartesian quartet by `mderi_screened` (lib/hf/md_eri), then `tr4_blocks`. The production build, `mderi_sph`, moves each quartet as it is computed; this is the path it is held to, with the same signature, `(atoms, shells, prims, M)`.

functions.name: tr4_block_sym_defect
functions.what: The per-quartet form computed for a shell quartet and for three of its symmetric images, (b a | d c), (c d | a b) and (d c | b a); the largest gap between matching entries. `tr4_blocks` computes only the canonical order, so this checks that the order it picks does not matter.

functions.name: ao_c2s
functions.what: The matrix that turns the molecule's Cartesian basis functions into spherical ones, `[nao_cart, nao_sph]`.

functions.name: ao_in_run
functions.what: A one-electron matrix over Cartesian functions in the run's functions: moved to spherical ones when the molecule is spherical, as it is otherwise.

functions.name: ao_overlap
functions.what: The overlap matrix S in the run's functions.

functions.name: ao_hcore
functions.what: The core Hamiltonian `H = T + V` in the run's functions.

functions.name: ao_eri
functions.what: The electron repulsion integrals, packed-8, in the run's functions, from the kernels lib/cas generated (lib/hf/mdg_eri). A spherical molecule's store holds spherical rows, so each quartet comes out spherical.

functions.name: eig_sort
functions.what: Sort the eigenvalues in `d` ascending, moving the columns of `V` with them. Selection sort: n is at most a few dozen, and a stable, simple order is what makes the members comparable.

functions.name: eig_fix_signs
functions.what: Flip each column of `V` so its largest-magnitude component is positive.

functions.name: eig_pack
functions.what: The member result `[n + 1, n]` from eigenvalues and vectors.

functions.name: eig_tred2
functions.what: Householder reduction of the symmetric matrix held in `V` to tridiagonal form (diagonal `d`, subdiagonal `e`), accumulating the transformation in `V`. JAMA's tred2 with `V` stored transposed: where JAMA reads `V[i, j]` this reads `V[j, i]`, so its inner loops, which run down a column, walk along a row of the row-major array. The arithmetic is JAMA's, term for term; only the storage is transposed.

functions.name: eig_tql2
functions.what: Implicit QL on the tridiagonal (`d`, `e`) from eig_tred2, rotating `V` (stored transposed, as eig_tred2 leaves it: row `k` is eigenvector `k`). JAMA's tql2. Returns the largest number of QL steps any one eigenvalue needed.

functions.name: eig_ql
functions.what: Member `0` (`EIG_QL`): Householder + QL.

functions.name: eig_jacobi_angle
functions.what: The rotation that zeroes the `(p, q)` entry of the symmetric block `[app apq; apq aqq]`: its cosine, sine and tangent, with the angle at most a quarter turn in magnitude.

functions.name: eig_jacobi_raw
functions.what: Cyclic Jacobi on a copy of `A`, pairs in row order (Golub and Van Loan's cyclic Jacobi). Fills `d` and `V` unsorted; returns the sweep count. A pair is set to zero without a rotation once it is too small to move an eigenvalue (Demmel and Veselic's relative test), and the iteration stops after a sweep that rotates nothing.

functions.name: eig_jacobi
functions.what: Member `1` (`EIG_JACOBI`): cyclic Jacobi.

functions.name: eig_builtin
functions.what: Member `2` (`EIG_BUILTIN`): the builtin `eig_sym`, sorted and sign-fixed like the others. It is a Jacobi code too, but written in Rust for the interpreter and in C for the compiled runtime, with rotation angles from atan2, cos and sin rather than the tangent formula above, and a different stopping rule (off-diagonal norm under `1e-12` times the Frobenius norm, checked before each sweep).

functions.name: eig_methods
functions.what: The eigensolver registry, production member first.

functions.name: eig_of
functions.what: The eigensolver `k` names on the symmetric `A[n, n]`: `[n + 1, n]`, row `0` the eigenvalues in ascending order, rows `1..n` the eigenvectors as columns. Each member is called by name, `eig_ql` (the production one) when `k` is the default.

functions.name: eig_values
functions.what: The eigenvalues of a member's result, `[n]`.

functions.name: eig_vectors
functions.what: The eigenvectors of a member's result, as the columns of `[n, n]`.

functions.name: eig_residual
functions.what: max |A V - V diag(vals)| over every entry, for a member result R.

functions.name: eig_orth_defect
functions.what: max |V^T V - I| for a member result R.

functions.name: eig_projector_gap
functions.what: max |P1 - P2| between the projectors onto the lowest `k` vectors of two member results. The projector is what an occupied space is, so it is the comparison that survives degenerate levels.

functions.name: eig_fnorm
functions.what: Frobenius norm of a square matrix.

functions.name: eig_random_sym
functions.what: Test helper: a symmetric `[n, n]` matrix with Park-Miller entries in $(-1, 1)$ from `seed`, so a failure can be quoted by its seed.

functions.name: eig_known_spectrum
functions.what: Test helper: Q diag(lam) Q^T for an orthogonal Q built from the vectors of a random matrix, so the spectrum is known exactly by construction (up to the rounding of the product).

functions.name: eig_agreement
functions.what: The worst member-to-member eigenvalue and projector gaps over the registry on one matrix, with k occupied vectors, and each member's worst residual and orthogonality defect.

functions.name: orth_threshold
functions.what: The threshold `orth_canon` uses: `opts[OPT_LINDEP]`, or `OPT_LINDEP_DEFAULT` when unset.

functions.name: orth_canon
functions.what: Member `ORTH_CANON`, the production one: canonical orthogonalization, columns with eigenvalue at or below the threshold dropped (kept columns first, in ascending order of their eigenvalue).

functions.name: orth_polish
functions.what: One Newton-Schulz step on the first m columns of X: X <- X (I - E/2) with E = X^T S X - I, so the new defect is of order E^2. The columns span the same space, so the SCF energy and density do not change. It matters when a kept eigenvalue of S is small, as on the diffuse H4 chain: the eigensolver's vectors are accurate only to about eps, and dividing by the square root of a small eigenvalue magnifies that error in X^T S X. E has to be formed with compensated sums (orth_gram_err) for the step to remove it [test "orth_canon drops exactly one vector on the diffuse H4 chain"].

functions.name: orth_prod_err
functions.what: The rounding error of p = fl(a b), so that a b = p + orth_prod_err(a, b, p) exactly (Dekker). The halves have at most half a double's significant bits, so every product of halves is exact and fusing one into an FMA changes nothing, which keeps the two engines in agreement.

functions.name: orth_gram_err
functions.what: E = X^T S X - I over the first m columns, as [m, m], each entry as accurate as a sum done in twice the working precision and then rounded. Every product carries its Dekker error and every addition its Knuth two-sum error. S x_b is kept as a hi + lo pair so the second product loses nothing either. Cost n^2 m + n m^2.

functions.name: orth_symm
functions.what: Member `ORTH_SYMM`: Lowdin's S^(-1/2).

functions.name: orth_cholesky
functions.what: The lower Cholesky factor L of S = L L^T.

functions.name: orth_chol
functions.what: Member `ORTH_CHOL`: X = L^(-T), by back substitution on L^T X = I.

functions.name: orth_sdot
functions.what: u^T S v for columns a of U and b of V.

functions.name: orth_gs
functions.what: Member `ORTH_GS`: Gram-Schmidt in the S inner product, two passes per vector.

functions.name: orth_methods
functions.what: The orthogonalizer registry, production member first.

functions.name: orth_rank
functions.what: Columns of X that are not all zero: the size m of the orthonormal space.

functions.name: orth_of
functions.what: The orthogonalizer `opts[OPT_ORTH]` names on S: `X[n, n]` with `X^T S X = I` over its first `orth_rank(X)` columns, the dropped columns zero. Each member is called by name, `orth_canon` (the production one) when the option is left at its default.

functions.name: orth_defect
functions.what: max |X^T S X - I| over the first m columns, formed with compensated sums so the measurement is not limited by its own rounding when X is large.

functions.name: orth_inverse_defect
functions.what: max |X X^T S - I|: X X^T is S^(-1) exactly when X has full rank.

functions.name: orth_check_all
functions.what: The worst X^T S X defect over the registry, and how many members did not keep exactly `mwant` columns, for one overlap matrix.

functions.name: den_stack1
functions.what: A `[1, n, n]` stack holding one matrix.

functions.name: den_stack2
functions.what: A `[2, n, n]` stack holding two matrices.

functions.name: den_from_vectors
functions.what: `w sum_(k = k0 .. k1-1) (X V[:, k]) (X V[:, k])^T`, `[n, n]`, with `X[n, m]` (its first m columns) and the eigenvectors `V[m, m]` as columns.

functions.name: den_fock
functions.what: The Fock matrices from J and K, `[nd, n, n]`: `H + J - K/2` for one total density, `H + J_a + J_b - K_s` for two spin densities.

functions.name: den_orth
functions.what: `X^T A X` over the first m columns of X: a matrix in the orthonormal basis.

functions.name: den_orth_density
functions.what: `X^T S D S X`: the density D in the orthonormal basis.

functions.name: den_orth_density_sx
functions.what: `U^T D U` with `U = S X` computed once: the density D in the orthonormal basis, for a loop that moves a new density there every iteration.

functions.name: den_commutator
functions.what: `F' P' - P' F'` for two `[m, m]` matrices: the SCF error in the orthonormal basis.

functions.name: den_commutator_sym
functions.what: `F' P' - P' F'` for two symmetric `[m, m]` matrices, as `A - A^T` with `A = F' P'`: one matrix product instead of two, since `(F' P')^T = P' F'` when both are symmetric. The result is antisymmetric to the bit. `den_commutator` is the definition term by term, and the test below holds the two together.

functions.name: den_maxabs
functions.what: The largest |entry| of a matrix.

functions.name: den_ao_commutator
functions.what: max |F D S - S D F| in the AO basis, for density d and Fock matrix f.

functions.name: den_trace
functions.what: Tr(D[d] S).

functions.name: den_trace2
functions.what: Tr(D[a] S D[b] S).

functions.name: den_idempotency
functions.what: max |D S D - w D| for density d.

functions.name: den_fnorm
functions.what: Frobenius norm of D[d].

functions.name: den_gap
functions.what: max |A[a] - B[b]| over two stacks of matrices.

functions.name: den_energy
functions.what: `E_nuc + (1/2) sum_d Tr(D_d (H + F_d))` over `ndens` densities.

functions.name: den_s2
functions.what: `<S^2>` of a UHF pair of spin densities D[0] (alpha), D[1] (beta).

functions.name: den_lowest
functions.what: Indices of the `k` smallest entries of `v`, ascending by value; entries whose `mask` is `1` are skipped. Ties go to the lower index.

functions.name: int_jk_is_direct
functions.what: `1` when J/K member `k` is one of the direct ones, which read a basis blob in place of packed integrals.

functions.name: int_basis_blob
functions.what: The basis blob that the direct members read (layout in the header). `M` is the c2s matrix for a spherical basis; pass `spherical = 0` for Cartesian, and then `M` is not read. The Schwarz factors of the shell pairs are computed here, once.

functions.name: int_blob_pack
functions.what: One `[rows, cols]` pack read back out of a blob, starting at `k0`.

functions.name: int_blob_basis
functions.what: The basis a blob holds, as a record (see the header for the layout).

functions.name: int_dens_cart
functions.what: The densities `D[nd, n, n]` in the Cartesian functions the integrals are computed in: `M D M^T` for a spherical basis, `D` as it is otherwise.

functions.name: int_jk_run
functions.what: Cartesian J and K `R[2 nd, nc, nc]` in the run's functions: `M^T R M` for a spherical basis, `R` as it is otherwise.

functions.name: int_jk_direct
functions.what: J/K member `INT_JK_DIRECT`, the production one: direct J and K from the basis blob in `X2`, screened by the Schwarz bound and the density, on the generated kernels in the run's functions (lib/hf/mdg_eri). `X1` and `X3` are not read.

functions.name: int_jk_direct_full
functions.what: J/K member `INT_JK_DIRECT_FULL`: direct J and K from the basis blob in `X2`, every quartet the Schwarz test keeps. `X1` and `X3` are not read.

functions.name: jk_packed
functions.what: Member `JK_PACKED`, the production one: one pass over the packed vector.

functions.name: jk_pairs
functions.what: Member `JK_PAIRS`: the integrals as a pair matrix.

functions.name: jk_dense
functions.what: Member `JK_DENSE`: the dense tensor and the definitions as written.

functions.name: jk_methods
functions.what: The J/K registry, production member first.

functions.name: jk_of
functions.what: J and K of the densities `D[ndens, n, n]`, `[2 ndens, n, n]`, by the member `opts[OPT_JK]` names: `jk_packed` (the production member), `jk_pairs`, `jk_dense`, or `int_jk_direct`, which reads the basis blob in `Gp`.

functions.name: jk_update
functions.what: J and K of the densities `D` from those of the densities `Dlast` they were last built from: `JKlast + JK(D - Dlast)`. J and K are linear in the density, so this is the whole build up to rounding and to what screening drops, and the direct member's density screening (lib/hf/md_direct) skips most quartets of a small change. The incremental Fock build of the SCF loop (lib/hf/scf_loop) calls it by name; PySCF's direct SCF builds its potential from `dm - dm_last` the same way (`get_veff`).

functions.name: jk_rebuild
functions.what: J and K of the densities `D` from the whole density, the last build unused: what `jk_update` is held to.

functions.name: jk_build_methods
functions.what: The ways to build the next J and K, the incremental one first.

functions.name: jk_t_opts
functions.what: The options array with J/K member `k` and the defaults.

functions.name: jk_rhf_energy
functions.what: The RHF energy of a reference total density, with J/K from member k: E_nuc + (1/2) Tr D (2H + J - K/2).

functions.name: jk_uhf_energy
functions.what: The UHF energy of reference spin densities, with J/K from member k.

functions.name: accel_capacity
functions.what: The ring capacity: opts[OPT_DIIS_N], at least `1`.

functions.name: accel_meta_new
functions.what: A fresh meta vector for a ring of capacity `nd`.

functions.name: accel_new
functions.what: An empty history for `k` matrices of `m x m` a step.

functions.name: accel_slot
functions.what: The ring slot holding the step `age` steps before the newest (age `0`).

functions.name: accel_push
functions.what: Store the newest Fock matrix `Fp[k, m, m]` and its error `Ep` in the ring. Returns the number of steps stored.

functions.name: accel_inner
functions.what: `<E, hist[slot]>` for an error `E` of the history's shape `[k, m, m]`: the one inner product the DIIS matrix is made of, so the kept and the recomputed `gram` agree to the bit. It is the `sum` of the elementwise product, not `dot` of the flattened arrays: in wasm `ravel` and `dot` go through the runtime bridge and cost more than the product itself (study/ports/pyscf FRICTION pyscf-022).

functions.name: accel_gram
functions.what: The inner products of every stored error pair, `[nd, nd]` by ring slot, recomputed from the history: what `accel_push` keeps in `gram`.

functions.name: accel_newest
functions.what: The newest Fock matrix, as a fresh `[ndens, m, m]` array.

functions.name: accel_solve
functions.what: Solve the k x k system A x = y in place by Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting; x overwrites y. Returns `1`, or `0` when a pivot is below `tol` times the largest entry of A (the system is then treated as singular and y is left unusable).

functions.name: accel_diis_coeffs
functions.what: DIIS coefficients over the newest `k` stored steps, from the inner products `G` of the stored errors (by ring slot): `1`, or `0` when the system is singular, and the coefficients `c[0..k-1]` (`c[t]` belongs to the step of age t).

functions.name: accel_cdiis_gram
functions.what: Commutator DIIS from the history and the inner products `G` of its errors. When the full history is singular it drops the oldest steps until the system solves; with one step it is plain iteration.

functions.name: accel_cdiis
functions.what: Member `ACCEL_CDIIS`, the production one: commutator DIIS, with the inner products recomputed from the history (`accel_extrapolate` passes the ones `accel_push` kept instead).

functions.name: accel_none
functions.what: Member `ACCEL_NONE`: plain iteration.

functions.name: accel_damp
functions.what: Member `ACCEL_DAMP`: damping against the matrix the previous step used.

functions.name: accel_methods
functions.what: The accelerator registry, production member first.

functions.name: accel_extrapolate
functions.what: The matrix the accelerator `opts[OPT_ACCEL]` names makes of the history, `[k, m, m]`; it is also recorded in slot `2 nd` as the matrix this step used. Each member is called by name, `accel_cdiis` (the production one) when the option is left at its default.

functions.name: accel_t_opts
functions.what: The options array with accelerator `k`, DIIS size `n` and the defaults.

functions.name: accel_t_system
functions.what: The matrix of the test problem, one row and column per unknown.

functions.name: accel_t_residual
functions.what: residual y - A x of the flattened x[0, :, :] into e[0, :, :]; returns its largest entry.

functions.name: accel_t_run
functions.what: Run `steps` Richardson steps under accelerator k; returns the final residual.

functions.name: gs_eig
functions.what: The eigen-decomposition of `X^T A X` (m columns of X kept) by eigensolver `opts[OPT_EIGEN]`: a member result, `[m + 1, m]` (lib/hf/eigen).

functions.name: gs_spins
functions.what: Spin densities `[2, n, n]` from the lowest `na` and `nb` eigenvectors in V.

functions.name: gs_occupy
functions.what: Occupy the lowest `na` and `nb` eigenvectors of `X^T A X` as spin densities.

functions.name: gs_fractional
functions.what: Occupation numbers for `N` electrons over the ascending levels `vals`: two per orbital from the bottom, and the electrons left for the partly filled level shared equally by every orbital within GS_AVG_DEGEN of it. Returns them and the number of orbitals with `f > 0`.

functions.name: gs_frac_density
functions.what: The total density `sum f_k c_k c_k^T` over the first `nocc` orbitals.

functions.name: gs_avg
functions.what: Member `GS_AVG`, the production one: the spin-averaged SCF, then aufbau per spin.

functions.name: gs_core
functions.what: Member `GS_CORE`: diagonalize the core Hamiltonian.

functions.name: gs_gwh_matrix
functions.what: The generalized Wolfsberg-Helmholz matrix.

functions.name: gs_gwh
functions.what: Member `GS_GWH`: generalized Wolfsberg-Helmholz.

functions.name: gs_zero
functions.what: Member `GS_ZERO`: nothing.

functions.name: gs_import
functions.what: Member `GS_IMPORT`: the caller's densities.

functions.name: gs_methods
functions.what: The guess registry, production member first.

functions.name: gs_of
functions.what: The starting spin densities `[2, n, n]` of the guess `opts[OPT_GUESS]` names. `D0` is what `gs_import` hands back. Each member is called by name, `gs_avg` (the production one) when the option is left at its default.

functions.name: rohf_feff
functions.what: The effective matrix `sum_xy Q_x (a_xy F_a + b_xy F_b) Q_y` over the closed, open and virtual projectors, `[1, m, m]`.

functions.name: rohf_c_gs
functions.what: Member 0: Guest-Saunders, PySCF's coupling.

functions.name: rohf_c_roothaan
functions.what: Member 1: Roothaan.

functions.name: rohf_c_mcweeny
functions.what: Member 2: McWeeny-Diercksen.

functions.name: rohf_c_bpd
functions.what: Member 3: Binkley-Pople-Dobosh.

functions.name: rohf_couplings
functions.what: The coupling registry, PySCF's first.

functions.name: rohf_effective
functions.what: The effective matrix `[1, m, m]` of coupling `opts[OPT_ROHF_COUPLING]`.

functions.name: rohf_error
functions.what: The ROHF error `Fe (P_c + P_o/2) - (P_c + P_o/2) Fe`, `[1, m, m]`, by the one-product commutator of lib/hf/density: the effective matrix is symmetrized when it is made and both projectors are symmetric.

functions.name: rohf_pick
functions.what: Which of the orbitals `V[m, m]` (columns) are closed and which open: `[2, m]`, row 0 the `nb` closed ones (lowest in `(F_a + F_b)/2`, ascending), row 1 the `na - nb` open ones (lowest in `F_a` among the rest).

functions.name: rohf_occupy
functions.what: The ROHF spin densities `[2, n, n]` of the orbitals `X V`: each closed orbital once in both, each open one once in `Da`, in the order picked.

functions.name: rohf_occupations
functions.what: The occupation of each orbital, `[m]`: 2 closed, 1 open, 0 virtual.

functions.name: rohf_level_shift
functions.what: The effective matrix `Fu[1, m, m]` with its virtual block raised by `shift`: `Fu + shift (I - P_c - P_o)`.

functions.name: scf_setup
functions.what: A setup from the matrices, the electron counts, the nuclear repulsion and the options.

functions.name: scf_setup_with
functions.what: The same setup with options `o`, its method decided again from them. A record update that changes the options' method or the electron counts would keep the old method; this and `scf_setup` are the ways to change them.

functions.name: scf_method
functions.what: The method options `o` ask for with `na` alpha and `nb` beta electrons: `o.method`, where automatic means RHF for equal spin counts and UHF otherwise. `scf_setup` asks it once and stores the answer in the setup.

functions.name: scf_opts
functions.what: The column array the registry members read (lib/hf/opts).

functions.name: scf_weight
functions.what: Electrons per orbital: two for the RHF total density, one for a spin density.

functions.name: scf_nocc
functions.what: The orbitals density d fills: `nalpha` for RHF and for alpha, `nbeta` for beta.

functions.name: scf_incremental
functions.what: The full-rebuild interval of the incremental Fock build: `fock_rebuild` when the run builds J and K with the production direct member, `0` (every build from the whole density) otherwise. In core a build costs the same whatever the density, so only the direct member gains from it.

functions.name: scf_nmatrix
functions.what: How many matrices DIIS extrapolates: one per density for RHF and UHF, the one effective matrix for ROHF.

functions.name: scf_swapped
functions.what: The same setup with the spin counts exchanged.

functions.name: scf_energy2
functions.what: The energy a second way, from J and K directly instead of from the Fock matrix: `E_nuc + Tr D H + (1/2) Tr D J - (1/4) Tr D K` for one total density, `E_nuc + Tr Dt H + (1/2) Tr Dt Jt - (1/2) sum_s Tr D_s K_s` for two.

functions.name: scf_commutator
functions.what: The Fock matrices and densities in the orthonormal basis of `X` (its `m` columns), the matrix DIIS extrapolates and its error. `U` is `S X`, which the loop computes once.

functions.name: scf_level_shift
functions.what: `Fnext` (the matrices about to be diagonalized, `[k, m, m]`) with the virtual orbitals raised by `shift`: `Fnext + shift (I - P'/w)` per spin for RHF and UHF, where `P'/w` projects on the occupied orbitals, and `Fnext + shift (I - P_c' - P_o')` for ROHF.

functions.name: scf_diagonalize
functions.what: The eigen-decomposition of each matrix of `Fnext`: a stack of eigensolver results, `[k, m + 1, m]` (lib/hf/eigen).

functions.name: scf_occupy
functions.what: The next densities from the eigenvectors in `eigs`: the lowest orbitals of each density for RHF and UHF, the closed and open ones for ROHF.

functions.name: scf_iterate
functions.what: The loop: iterate from the densities `D0` (`[1, n, n]` for RHF, `[2, n, n]` otherwise) until the energy and the commutator settle, or `max_iter` iterations have run.

functions.name: scf_coefficients
functions.what: `X V`: orbitals as AO coefficients, `[n, m]`.

functions.name: scf_aufbau
functions.what: The aufbau occupations of `m` orbitals with `nocc` filled, `w` each.

functions.name: scf_orbitals
functions.what: The orbitals of one Fock matrix `Fd[n, n]`: its eigenvectors in the orthonormal basis of `X`, the lowest `nocc` filled with `w` electrons each.

functions.name: scf_result
functions.what: The result record of a run that ended with densities D, Fock matrices F (and their J and K) built from the densities before them, energy e, convergence flag `conv` and `it` iterations.

functions.name: scf_unswap
functions.what: The same result with the two spins exchanged.

functions.name: scf_solve
functions.what: The one way into the loop: iterate from spin densities `start[2, n, n]` (in the setup's spin order) with the method the setup asks for.

functions.name: scf
functions.what: The SCF of a setup: from the guess `setup.options.guess`, the method the setup asks for, iterated until it converges.

functions.name: scf_run_from
functions.what: From the spin densities `Da` and `Db` (for RHF, any split of the total density, such as half of it each).

functions.name: scf_step
functions.what: One plain step from `Da`, `Db`: build F, diagonalize, occupy, with no extrapolation and no level shift. The result's energy and Fock matrices are those of the densities given; its densities are the new ones.

functions.name: scf_densities
functions.what: The spin densities of a result as the `[nd, n, n]` stack the loop carries: the total density for RHF, alpha then beta otherwise.

functions.name: scf_density_gap
functions.what: The largest difference between two results' densities: the total density for RHF, spin by spin otherwise.

functions.name: scf_t_model
functions.what: Test helper: PySCF's atom-free model (test_rhf.py:757, test_uhf.py:374): a diagonal h, S = I, one on-site integral (ii|ii) per orbital, no nuclei.

functions.name: scf_blob
functions.what: The basis blob the direct J/K member reads (lib/hf/jk_direct).

functions.name: scf_run_options
functions.what: The options a run uses: a direct run starts from the core Hamiltonian when it asks for the averaged guess, which needs packed integrals.

functions.name: scf_setup_of
functions.what: A setup from integrals computed elsewhere: the molecule gives the electron counts and the nuclear repulsion.

functions.name: integrals
functions.what: The setup of a run on molecule `mol` with options `o`: its integrals, each by its production member, its electron counts and its nuclear repulsion. A direct run (`o.jk = INT_JK_DIRECT` or `INT_JK_DIRECT_FULL`) gets the basis blob in place of the packed integrals.

functions.name: scf_with
functions.what: Hartree-Fock with options `o`.

functions.name: rhf
functions.what: Restricted Hartree-Fock with the production options.

functions.name: uhf
functions.what: Unrestricted Hartree-Fock with the production options.

functions.name: rohf
functions.what: Restricted open-shell Hartree-Fock with the production options.

functions.name: stab_orbitals
functions.what: The orbital pack `[nd, n + 1, m]` of the densities `D[nd, n, n]`: the eigenvectors of `F(D)` in the orthonormal basis `X`, as AO coefficients, with the aufbau occupation flags in row n.

functions.name: stab_split
functions.what: Occupied MO indices of spin d into `idx[d, 0 .. no-1]`, then the virtual ones into `idx[d, no .. m-1]`. Returns `no`.

functions.name: stab_nparam
functions.what: Number of rotation parameters: `sum_d no_d (m - no_d)`.

functions.name: stab_density
functions.what: The densities of an orbital pack, `[nd, n, n]`: `2 C_occ C_occ^T` for one closed-shell set, `C_s,occ C_s,occ^T` per spin for two.

functions.name: stab_fock_mo
functions.what: The Fock matrices of an orbital pack in its own MO basis, `[nd, m, m]`: `C_d^T F_d C_d` with `F` built from the pack's densities.

functions.name: stab_mo_eri
functions.what: `(pq|rs)` in the MO basis, `[m, m, m, m]`, with `p, q` orbitals of spin s and `r, s` of spin t, from the dense AO tensor `G[n, n, n, n]`. Four quarter transforms, each `m n^4` or less.

functions.name: stab_fill_block
functions.what: Fill the (s, t) block of the Hessian from the MO integrals `M` of that spin pair; `nd = 1` uses the RHF formula. Returns `0`.

functions.name: stab_layout
functions.what: Offsets of each spin's parameters into `off`, occupied counts into `no` and the index lists into `idx`. Returns the parameter count.

functions.name: stab_hess_mo
functions.what: Hessian member `0` (production): the explicit formulas from MO integrals.

functions.name: stab_hop
functions.what: `Hess kappa` without MO integrals: one J/K build on the AO matrices `X_d = C_d (kappa_d + kappa_d^T) C_d^T`. `Fm` is `stab_fock_mo(orb, ...)` and the layout arrays come from `stab_layout`.

functions.name: stab_hess_jk
functions.what: Hessian member `1`: column k is `Hess e_k`, from `stab_hop`.

functions.name: stab_hess_methods
functions.what: The Hessian registry, production member first.

functions.name: stab_hessian
functions.what: The Hessian of an orbital pack from member `p.options.stab_hessian`.

functions.name: stab_gradient
functions.what: The gradient `dE/dkappa` of an orbital pack, in the Hessian's layout: `4 F_ai` (RHF) or `2 F^s_ai` (UHF).

functions.name: stab_expm
functions.what: `exp(K)` for a square `K`, by scaling and squaring: halve K until its largest absolute row sum is at most 1/4, sum `STAB_EXPM_TERMS` Taylor terms after the identity (the first term left out is at most `0.25^19 / 19! = 3e-29` there), then square back.

functions.name: stab_rotate
functions.what: The orbital pack rotated by `C_d exp(t K_d)` per spin, where `K_d` holds `kap` in the Hessian's layout. The occupation row is copied.

functions.name: stab_energy_d
functions.what: The energy of the densities `D[nd, n, n]`.

functions.name: stab_energy
functions.what: The energy of the determinant(s) of an orbital pack.

functions.name: stab_energy_along
functions.what: The energy after rotating the pack by `t kap`.

functions.name: stab_curvature
functions.what: `d^2 E(C exp(t K)) / dt^2` at `t = 0` by central differences with steps h and 2h, combined by Richardson extrapolation so the error is O(h^4).

functions.name: stab_slope
functions.what: `dE(C exp(t K)) / dt` at `t = 0`, central differences with Richardson.

functions.name: stab_quad
functions.what: `v^T A v`.

functions.name: stab_lowest
functions.what: The lowest eigenvalue of the symmetric `Hs` and its unit eigenvector, from eigensolver `options.eigensolver`.

functions.name: stab_label
functions.what: STAB_STABLE when `lam` is above -STAB_TOL, STAB_DEFAULT otherwise.

functions.name: stab_line_min
functions.what: The step along `kap` with the lowest energy on the grid `+-STAB_DT * (1 .. STAB_NSTEP)`; ties go to the earlier point, positive steps first.

functions.name: stab_lowest_of
functions.what: The lowest Hessian eigenvalue of the densities `D[nd, n, n]`, and its eigenvector.

functions.name: stab_follow
functions.what: Stability analysis and follow-down from the converged densities `D0[nd, n, n]`. Every restart is an SCF (lib/hf/scf_loop) under the setup's options.

functions.name: stab_run
functions.what: `stab_follow` from an SCF result.

functions.name: casida_ab
functions.what: A and B for singlets (`spin` = 0) or triplets (`spin` = 1), written into A and B from the orbital energies and the MO integrals.

functions.name: matmul_into
functions.what: C = X Y for square matrices.

functions.name: tda_energies
functions.what: The TDA energies: the eigenvalues of A, ascending.

functions.name: tdhf_energies
functions.what: The TDHF energies: omega = sqrt(lambda) for the eigenvalues lambda of (A - B)^(1/2) (A + B) (A - B)^(1/2). Returns -1 in place of the energies if A - B is not positive definite.

functions.name: max_gap
functions.what: The largest |x_k - y_k|.

posts.title: Excitation energies of water from the Casida equation, with and without de-excitations
posts.titleHtml: Excitation energies of water from the Casida equation, with and without de-excitations

posts.summaryHtml: Water in the 6-31G basis, from its Hartree-Fock ground state to all 40 singlet and 40 triplet excitation energies, two ways. Time-dependent Hartree-Fock (the random-phase approximation) keeps the coupling B between excitations and de-excitations; the Tamm-Dancoff approximation drops it and diagonalizes A alone. The lowest singlet is at 0.344074 Ha (9.363 eV) in TDHF and 0.346161 Ha in TDA, and every one of the 160 energies matches PySCF's to 10−8 Ha.
posts.summaryText: Water in the 6-31G basis, from its Hartree-Fock ground state to all 40 singlet and 40 triplet excitation energies, two ways. Time-dependent Hartree-Fock (the random-phase approximation) keeps the coupling B between excitations and de-excitations; the Tamm-Dancoff approximation drops it and diagonalizes A alone. The lowest singlet is at 0.344074 Ha (9.363 eV) in TDHF and 0.346161 Ha in TDA, and every one of the 160 energies matches PySCF's to 10^-8 Ha.
notes: A molecule absorbs light at the energies of its excited states above the ground state, its excitation energies. Hartree-Fock gives only the ground state, a single set of occupied orbitals. Linear response asks how that state responds to a weak oscillating field: the response diverges at frequencies ω that solve the eigenvalue problem above, the Casida equation. The unknowns are the amplitudes Xia​ for moving an electron from an occupied orbital i to a virtual one a, and Yia​ for the reverse.
For a closed-shell molecule with real orbitals, orbital energies ε, and two-electron integrals (pq∣rs) in the molecular-orbital basis (chemists' notation),
Aia,jb​=δij​δab​(εa​−εi​)+2(ia∣jb)−(ij∣ab),Bia,jb​=2(ia∣jb)−(ib∣ja)

for singlets. For triplets the Coulomb terms 2(ia∣jb) drop out, since a spin flip moves no net charge. With B the equation is time-dependent Hartree-Fock (TDHF), also called the random-phase approximation (RPA). With B=0 only A is left, and its eigenvalues are the Tamm-Dancoff (TDA) energies, the same as configuration interaction with single excitations.

The program computes the integrals, the ground state and both spectra in this file, with lib/hf for the integrals and the self-consistent field. The reference is PySCF 2.5.0 (posts/refs/casida-tdhf-and-tda-for-water.py), which shares no code with it and solves both problems by Davidson iteration on matrix-vector products, without building A or B.
posts.equation: \begin{pmatrix} A & B \\ -B & -A \end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix} X \\ Y \end{pmatrix} = \omega\begin{pmatrix} X \\ Y \end{pmatrix}, \qquad (A - B)^{1/2}(A + B)(A - B)^{1/2}\, Z = \omega^2 Z
posts.equationHtml: (A−B​B−A​)(XY​)=ω(XY​),(A−B)1/2(A+B)(A−B)1/2Z=ω2Z
posts.source:
from hf.mole import molecule
from hf.molecule import mol_nelectron
from hf.scf import integrals
from hf.eri_store import es_unpack8
from hf.scf_loop import scf, scf_densities
from hf.opts import scf_defaults
from hf.stab import stab_fock_mo, stab_mo_eri, stab_orbitals

###
## The ground state and its orbitals

The molecule is PySCF's water, written as PySCF takes it, and the 6-31G
basis is found by its name in the table `lib/basis/pople631g`: 13 basis functions, 5 doubly occupied orbitals and 8
virtual ones, so $5 \times 8 = 40$ occupied-virtual pairs. The RHF energy
matches PySCF's $-75.98394849810573$ Ha. The orbitals are the eigenvectors of
the converged Fock matrix, and the integrals $(pq|rs)$ over them come from
four quarter-transformations of the atomic-orbital integrals.
###

water = molecule("O 0 0 0; H 0 -0.757 0.587; H 0 0.757 0.587", "6-31g")
setup = integrals(water, scf_defaults())
H = setup.h
G = setup.eri
ground = scf(setup)
E_rhf = ground.energy
show E_rhf
nbf = len(H)
orb = stab_orbitals(setup, scf_densities(ground))
Fmo = stab_fock_mo(orb, H, G)
mo_eri = stab_mo_eri(es_unpack8(G, nbf), orb, 0, 0)
nocc = round(mol_nelectron(water) / 2)
nvir = nbf - nocc
nov = nocc * nvir
eps = zeros(nbf)
for p to nbf {
    eps[p] = Fmo[0, p, p]
}
show eps

test "the RHF energy is PySCF's -75.98394849810573 to 1e-9" {
    assert_near(E_rhf, -75.98394849810573, 1.0e-9)
}

###
## Building $A$ and $B$, and solving

The pair $ia$ is stored at index $i \cdot n_\text{vir} + (a - n_\text{occ})$.

TDA is one symmetric eigenvalue problem, $A\,X = \omega X$.

For TDHF the $2n \times 2n$ problem is not symmetric, but it folds into a
symmetric one of size $n$. Adding and subtracting its two block rows gives
$(A + B)(X + Y) = \omega(X - Y)$ and $(A - B)(X - Y) = \omega(X + Y)$, so
$(A - B)(A + B)(X + Y) = \omega^2(X + Y)$. When $A - B$ is positive definite,
which holds when the Hartree-Fock state is stable against these rotations,
it has a square root, and $Z = (A - B)^{-1/2}(X + Y)$ turns the product into
the symmetric matrix under the title. Its eigenvalues are $\omega^2$.

All 160 energies agree with PySCF's to $3.7\times10^{-9}$ Ha, about what is
left of the self-consistent field's convergence; the tests allow $10^{-8}$.
###

#| A and B for singlets (`spin` = 0) or triplets (`spin` = 1), written
#| into A and B from the orbital energies and the MO integrals.
def casida_ab(eps: Arr, M: Arr, nocc, nvir, spin, A: Arr, B: Arr) {
    coul = 2.0
    if spin > 0.5 {
        coul = 0.0
    }
    for i to nocc {
        for a to nvir {
            ia = i * nvir + a
            for j to nocc {
                for b to nvir {
                    jb = j * nvir + b
                    A[ia, jb] = coul * M[i, nocc + a, j, nocc + b] - M[i, j, nocc + a, nocc + b]
                    B[ia, jb] = coul * M[i, nocc + a, j, nocc + b] - M[i, nocc + b, j, nocc + a]
                }
            }
            A[ia, ia] += eps[nocc + a] - eps[i]
        }
    }
    return 0
}

#| C = X Y for square matrices.
def matmul_into(X: Arr, Y: Arr, C: Arr) {
    n = len(X)
    for i to n {
        for j to n {
            s = 0.0
            for k to n {
                s += X[i, k] * Y[k, j]
            }
            C[i, j] = s
        }
    }
    return 0
}

#| The TDA energies: the eigenvalues of A, ascending.
def tda_energies(A: Arr) {
    n = len(A)
    w = zeros(n)
    V = zeros(n, n)
    eig_sym(A + 0.0, w, V)
    sort(w)
    return w
}

#| The TDHF energies: omega = sqrt(lambda) for the eigenvalues lambda
#| of (A - B)^(1/2) (A + B) (A - B)^(1/2). Returns -1 in place of the
#| energies if A - B is not positive definite.
def tdhf_energies(A: Arr, B: Arr) {
    n = len(A)
    w = zeros(n)
    V = zeros(n, n)
    eig_sym(A - B, w, V)
    if min(w) <= 0.0 {
        return zeros(n) - 1.0
    }
    R = zeros(n, n)
    for i to n {
        for j to n {
            s = 0.0
            for k to n {
                s += V[i, k] * sqrt(w[k]) * V[j, k]
            }
            R[i, j] = s
        }
    }
    T = zeros(n, n)
    C = zeros(n, n)
    matmul_into(A + B, R, T)
    matmul_into(R, T, C)
    lam = zeros(n)
    eig_sym(C, lam, V)
    om = zeros(n)
    for k to n {
        om[k] = sqrt(lam[k])
    }
    sort(om)
    return om
}

A_s = zeros(nov, nov)
B_s = zeros(nov, nov)
casida_ab(eps, mo_eri, nocc, nvir, 0, A_s, B_s)
A_t = zeros(nov, nov)
B_t = zeros(nov, nov)
casida_ab(eps, mo_eri, nocc, nvir, 1, A_t, B_t)
s_tda = tda_energies(A_s)
s_tdhf = tdhf_energies(A_s, B_s)
t_tda = tda_energies(A_t)
t_tdhf = tdhf_energies(A_t, B_t)
HARTREE_EV = 27.211386245988
lowest_singlet_ev = s_tdhf[0] * HARTREE_EV
show nov
show lowest_singlet_ev

###
## What $B$ does

$B$ couples each excitation to the de-excitations, and its effect is to
pull the energies down. For the lowest root this always holds. With
$\Lambda = \begin{pmatrix} A & B \\ B & A \end{pmatrix}$, the lowest TDHF $\omega$ is the minimum
of $(X, Y)^T\Lambda(X, Y)/(X^TX - Y^TY)$ over vectors with $X^TX > Y^TY$;
the vectors with $Y = 0$ are among them, and over those the ratio is
$X^TAX/X^TX$, whose minimum is the lowest TDA energy. For water every root comes out lower in TDHF than in TDA,
by 0.07 to 63 millihartree for the singlets and 0.01 to 19 for the triplets
(`posts/refs` prints the same ranges from PySCF); the largest is the 25th
singlet's, 63 millihartree. The 8 roots near 20 Ha, which move an electron
out of the oxygen 1s orbital, shift by less than 0.25 millihartree.

The triplets sit below the singlets. The singlet $A$ and $B$ carry the extra
term $2(ia|jb)$, whose diagonal $2(ia|ia)$ is the Coulomb self-repulsion of
the charge distribution $\phi_i\phi_a$ and is positive.
The lowest triplet is 0.3065 Ha, 1.023 eV below the lowest singlet.

The first figure shows the 32 valence excitation energies of each kind.
The second shows, root by root, how far TDA lies above TDHF.
###

s_shift = s_tda - s_tdhf

posts.summaryHtml: Two capacitors, an inductor, a resistor and one diode whose current is a three-piece straight line. The voltages never settle and never repeat: they wind around two centers, hopping between them at irregular times. Nearby starts separate like eλt with λ=0.33, which is what a separate scipy calculation gives within the scatter expected of a run this long.
posts.summaryText: Two capacitors, an inductor, a resistor and one diode whose current is a three-piece straight line. The voltages never settle and never repeat: they wind around two centers, hopping between them at irregular times. Nearby starts separate like e^(λ t) with λ = 0.33, which is what a separate scipy calculation gives within the scatter expected of a run this long.
notes: The exponent is measured here by following two copies of the circuit started 10−8 apart and pulling them back to that distance after every step (Benettin's method). The reference, in posts/refs/chuas-circuit-double-scroll.py, uses a different method and a different integrator: scipy's DOP853 at a tolerance of 10−11, carrying the linearized equations along the orbit, over 24000 time units. It gives λ=0.3277±0.0026. Split into 40 windows of 600 time units (the length of this post's run), the estimates scatter with a standard deviation of 0.0165, so the test allows three of those: 0.05.
