functions.name: mdg_rfill
functions.what: `herm_rfill` for `L <= MDG_RMAX` by the def of its class; `-1` and nothing written above it (no `stop`, so that a `parallel for` may call it).

functions.name: mdg_pair
functions.what: The pair expansion of a `(la, lb)` pair, `la, lb <= MDG_LMAX`, by the def of its class; `-1` and nothing written above it.

functions.name: mdg_gather
functions.what: The gather of a ket pair of total order `L2 <= 2 MDG_LMAX` by the def of its order; `-1` and nothing written above it.

functions.name: mdg_t2
functions.what: The pair transform `(M_a (x) M_b)^T`, `[nsph_a nsph_b, ncart_a ncart_b]`, from the c2s blocks of shells `sa` and `sb` in the block-diagonal `M`.

functions.name: mdg_pair_general
functions.what: `mdg_pair` for a class with no generated kernel: the same entries from `herm_etab` (lib/hf/hermite) in loops, into the flat `V`.

functions.name: mdg_fillpack
functions.what: The E matrix of the group pair of `nga` shells from `sa` and `ngb` from `sb`; its primitive pairs' `(p, Px, Py, Pz)` into `ST` at `off` (md_eri's pack header and primitive list) and its row index at `ix`. With `sph = 1` the rows are spherical, `T` the pair transform; else Cartesian and `T` is not read.

functions.name: mdg_nrows
functions.what: The rows of pair `k` of the store: shells in the two groups times functions per shell pair.

functions.name: mdg_pick
functions.what: Entry `i` of `A` followed by `B`.

functions.name: mdg_packs
functions.what: The E matrices of store pairs `k0 .. k0 + n - 1`, filling their packs in `ST` as it goes. Built by halves: a loop that appended every pair's record would keep all the arrays made so far, and the C runtime checks each array it frees at the end of an iteration against those it keeps (`viv_arena_release_kept`), which made the loop quadratic in the pairs (study/ports/pyscf/FRICTION.json, pyscf-024).

functions.name: mdg_store
functions.what: The store over every canonical pair of md_eri's shell groups: md_eri's directory and pack headers in `ST` (no E entries) followed by the pairs' row indices, and each pair's E matrix in `EM`. `M` is the c2s matrix when `sph = 1`.

functions.name: mdg_htab
functions.what: md_eri's `mderi_hoff` for every case a build with shells up to `lmax` meets, made once, as one flat table with rows of `herm_nh(2 lmax)`. With `nl = 4 lmax + 1` totals and `lp = 2 lmax + 1` pair orders, row `Ls nl + L` holds the cube offsets `(t D + u) D + v`, `D = L + 1`, of the Hermite list of order `Ls`, and row `lp nl + Ls` the signs `(-1)^(t+u+v)`.

functions.name: mdg_put
functions.what: Write block `B` of store pairs `(k1, k2)` into the packed vector, the canonical entries only, as md_eri's `mderi_put_at` does, through the pairs' row indices in `ST`.

functions.name: mdg_block
functions.what: The block `(ab|cd)` for bra pair `k1` and ket pair `k2`, `[rows of k1, rows of k2]`, in the store's functions (spherical or Cartesian). `G` is from `mderi_grid`, `HT` from `mdg_htab`. md_eri's `mderi_block` with the generated R kernel, the kept E matrices and the offset tables made once.

functions.name: mdg_gather_general
functions.what: The general gather of one primitive quartet's Hermite values: `BR[o + hc ncol + ha] = sign(hc) S[offset(hc) + offset(ha)]`, the offsets and signs read from `mdg_htab`'s table (`ia`, `ic` and `isg` where the bra offsets, the ket offsets and the ket signs start). The generated `mdg_gather` does the same with the ket offsets as constants; this def runs the orders above it and checks it (the test below).

functions.name: mdg_schwarz
functions.what: `Q[k] = sqrt(max (ab|ab))` over the rows of store pair `k`.

functions.name: mdg_schwarz_one
functions.what: `Q[k]` for one store pair; a def of its own so its block is freed on return.

functions.name: mdg_do
functions.what: One row of the quartet list, computed and written; a def of its own so its arrays are freed on return.

functions.name: mdg_build
functions.what: Packed-8 ERIs, Schwarz-screened at `tol` (a negative `tol` skips nothing), over spherical functions when `sph = 1` (`M` the c2s matrix) and Cartesian ones otherwise.

functions.name: mdg_sph
functions.what: The production ERIs over spherical functions, `M` the c2s matrix of lib/hf/cart2sph: Schwarz-screened at `MDERI_SCREEN_TOL`.

functions.name: mdg_screened
functions.what: The production ERIs over unit-normalized Cartesian functions, Schwarz-screened at `MDERI_SCREEN_TOL`: the integral-stage member `(atoms, shells, prims) -> packed-8`.

functions.name: mdg_jk_put
functions.what: Add block `B` of store pairs `(k1, k2)` into the J and K copies `W[w0 + 2d]` (J) and `W[w0 + 2d + 1]` (K) of each density `d`: md_direct's `mdjk_put` through the rows' function indices in `ST`.

functions.name: mdg_dmax
functions.what: md_direct's `mdjk_dmax` over spherical functions when `sph = 1` and Cartesian ones otherwise: the largest `|D|` over the functions of each pair of shell groups, `[ng, ng]`.

functions.name: mdg_jk_pair
functions.what: One quartet computed and added into `W`; a def of its own so the block is freed as soon as it has been added.

functions.name: mdg_jk_chunk
functions.what: Chunk `c` of `nch`: md_direct's `mdjk_chunk_screened` on this module's quartets. Bra pairs `c, c + nch, ...`, each against every ket pair up to it, a quartet kept when it passes the Schwarz test (`Q_AB Q_CD >= tol_s`) and the density test.

functions.name: mdg_schwarz_basis
functions.what: The Schwarz factors of the store `mdg_jk_screened` builds, over spherical functions when `sph = 1` (`M` the c2s matrix): a property of the basis, computed once per SCF (lib/hf/jk_direct's blob).

functions.name: mdg_jk_screened
functions.what: J and K of the densities `D[nd, n, n]` in the run's functions (spherical when `sph = 1`, `M` the c2s matrix; Cartesian otherwise), Schwarz and density screened, from the Schwarz factors `Q` of `mdg_schwarz_basis`; `[2 nd, n, n]`, J then K per density.

functions.name: c2s_binom
functions.what: n choose k, exact in doubles for the small arguments used here.

functions.name: c2s_unit_gram
functions.what: The overlap of the unit Cartesian components of one shell, `[ncart, ncart]`, when they share one radial part. Per axis the Gaussian moment gives `(p + q - 1)!!` for powers p and q with p + q even, and 0 when it is odd; the unit factors `Nc` scale the result so the diagonal is 1.

functions.name: c2s_cart_row
functions.what: The row of component (lx, ly, lz) in PySCF's Cartesian order: the components with a larger lx come first, and within one lx a larger ly.

functions.name: c2s_closed
functions.what: M_l by hand for l <= 3. Rows are the unit Cartesian components in PySCF's order, columns the spherical functions in PySCF's order. Each entry is a coefficient of the polynomial named above it times sqrt((2lx-1)!! (2ly-1)!! (2lz-1)!!), divided by the polynomial's norm. Above l = 3 it returns `c2s_general(l)`.

functions.name: c2s_sph_col
functions.what: The column of the spherical function with index m in PySCF's order. For p PySCF keeps x, y, z, which are m = 1, -1, 0.

functions.name: c2s_general
functions.what: M_l for any l from the real solid harmonic expansion  S_lm ~ sum_t sum_u sum_w (-1)^(t + (w - wm)/2) 4^-t C(l,t) C(l-t,|m|+t) C(t,u) C(|m|,w) x^(2t + |m| - 2u - w) y^(2u + w) z^(l - 2t - |m|)  with t = 0 .. (l - |m|)/2, u = 0 .. t, and w running over the integers up to |m| that are even for m >= 0 and odd for m < 0 (wm is 0 or 1 to match). This is Helgaker's sum with v = w/2. The overall constant is left out: each column is scaled afterwards to unit norm in the metric of `c2s_unit_gram`, which also converts monomial coefficients to unit ones.

functions.name: c2s_block
functions.what: The production M_l: the hand-written table where it exists, the general construction above it.

functions.name: c2s_basis
functions.what: The block-diagonal M for a basis, `[nao_cart, nao_sph]`: shell s puts its M_l at rows SH_CART0 and columns SH_SPH0, and everything between shells is zero. Then PySCF's spherical X is `M^T X_unit M`.

functions.name: c2s_orth_gap
functions.what: The largest entry of abs(M^T G M - I) for one block.

functions.name: tr2_dense
functions.what: `M^T X M` as two full matrix products, `[nao_sph, nao_sph]`. The shells pack is used only for the two sizes.

functions.name: tr2_blocks
functions.what: `M^T X M` one shell pair at a time: the (a, b) spherical block is `M_a^T X_ab M_b`, where `M_a` is shell a's diagonal block of M. Every pair is done, so X need not be symmetric.

functions.name: tr2_back_dense
functions.what: `M D M^T`, `[nao_cart, nao_cart]`: a spherical density as the Cartesian one with the same contractions, since Tr(D M^T X M) = Tr((M D M^T) X).

functions.name: tr2_back_blocks
functions.what: `M D M^T` one shell pair at a time.

functions.name: tr4_dense
functions.what: The dense four-index transform of a dense `[nc, nc, nc, nc]` tensor, one index per pass: l, then k, then j, then i. Returns `[ns, ns, ns, ns]`.

functions.name: tr4_quarter
functions.what: Packed Cartesian ERIs to packed spherical ones through the dense view and four quarter transformations. Meant for n <= 30, like `es_unpack8`.

functions.name: tr4_quartet
functions.what: The spherical block `[ma, mb, mc, md]` of shells (a, b, c, d), from the Cartesian block read out of the packed vector and the four `M_l` blocks. Any order of the four shells works, because `es_index8` accepts any order. A shell up to p is the same in both sets, so its pass is skipped.

functions.name: tr4_blocks
functions.what: Packed Cartesian ERIs to packed spherical ones, one canonical shell quartet at a time: a >= b, c >= d and pair(a, b) >= pair(c, d). Every canonical spherical (pq|rs) lies in one of those quartets, since the symmetry that maps a function quartet to its canonical order maps its shell quartet the same way.

functions.name: tr4_two_pass
functions.what: The ERIs over spherical functions in two passes: every Cartesian quartet by `mderi_screened` (lib/hf/md_eri), then `tr4_blocks`. The production build, `mderi_sph`, moves each quartet as it is computed; this is the path it is held to, with the same signature, `(atoms, shells, prims, M)`.

functions.name: tr4_block_sym_defect
functions.what: The per-quartet form computed for a shell quartet and for three of its symmetric images, (b a | d c), (c d | a b) and (d c | b a); the largest gap between matching entries. `tr4_blocks` computes only the canonical order, so this checks that the order it picks does not matter.

functions.name: ao_c2s
functions.what: The matrix that turns the molecule's Cartesian basis functions into spherical ones, `[nao_cart, nao_sph]`.

functions.name: ao_in_run
functions.what: A one-electron matrix over Cartesian functions in the run's functions: moved to spherical ones when the molecule is spherical, as it is otherwise.

functions.name: ao_overlap
functions.what: The overlap matrix S in the run's functions.

functions.name: ao_hcore
functions.what: The core Hamiltonian `H = T + V` in the run's functions.

functions.name: ao_eri
functions.what: The electron repulsion integrals, packed-8, in the run's functions, from the kernels lib/cas generated (lib/hf/mdg_eri). A spherical molecule's store holds spherical rows, so each quartet comes out spherical.

functions.name: eig_sort
functions.what: Sort the eigenvalues in `d` ascending, moving the columns of `V` with them. Selection sort: n is at most a few dozen, and a stable, simple order is what makes the members comparable.

functions.name: eig_fix_signs
functions.what: Flip each column of `V` so its largest-magnitude component is positive.

functions.name: eig_pack
functions.what: The member result `[n + 1, n]` from eigenvalues and vectors.

functions.name: eig_tred2
functions.what: Householder reduction of the symmetric matrix held in `V` to tridiagonal form (diagonal `d`, subdiagonal `e`), accumulating the transformation in `V`. JAMA's tred2 with `V` stored transposed: where JAMA reads `V[i, j]` this reads `V[j, i]`, so its inner loops, which run down a column, walk along a row of the row-major array. The arithmetic is JAMA's, term for term; only the storage is transposed.

functions.name: eig_tql2
functions.what: Implicit QL on the tridiagonal (`d`, `e`) from eig_tred2, rotating `V` (stored transposed, as eig_tred2 leaves it: row `k` is eigenvector `k`). JAMA's tql2. Returns the largest number of QL steps any one eigenvalue needed.

functions.name: eig_ql
functions.what: Member `0` (`EIG_QL`): Householder + QL.

functions.name: eig_jacobi_angle
functions.what: The rotation that zeroes the `(p, q)` entry of the symmetric block `[app apq; apq aqq]`: its cosine, sine and tangent, with the angle at most a quarter turn in magnitude.

functions.name: eig_jacobi_raw
functions.what: Cyclic Jacobi on a copy of `A`, pairs in row order (Golub and Van Loan's cyclic Jacobi). Fills `d` and `V` unsorted; returns the sweep count. A pair is set to zero without a rotation once it is too small to move an eigenvalue (Demmel and Veselic's relative test), and the iteration stops after a sweep that rotates nothing.

functions.name: eig_jacobi
functions.what: Member `1` (`EIG_JACOBI`): cyclic Jacobi.

functions.name: eig_builtin
functions.what: Member `2` (`EIG_BUILTIN`): the builtin `eig_sym`, sorted and sign-fixed like the others. It is a Jacobi code too, but written in Rust for the interpreter and in C for the compiled runtime, with rotation angles from atan2, cos and sin rather than the tangent formula above, and a different stopping rule (off-diagonal norm under `1e-12` times the Frobenius norm, checked before each sweep).

functions.name: eig_methods
functions.what: The eigensolver registry, production member first.

functions.name: eig_of
functions.what: The eigensolver `k` names on the symmetric `A[n, n]`: `[n + 1, n]`, row `0` the eigenvalues in ascending order, rows `1..n` the eigenvectors as columns. Each member is called by name, `eig_ql` (the production one) when `k` is the default.

functions.name: eig_values
functions.what: The eigenvalues of a member's result, `[n]`.

functions.name: eig_vectors
functions.what: The eigenvectors of a member's result, as the columns of `[n, n]`.

functions.name: eig_residual
functions.what: max |A V - V diag(vals)| over every entry, for a member result R.

functions.name: eig_orth_defect
functions.what: max |V^T V - I| for a member result R.

functions.name: eig_projector_gap
functions.what: max |P1 - P2| between the projectors onto the lowest `k` vectors of two member results. The projector is what an occupied space is, so it is the comparison that survives degenerate levels.

functions.name: eig_fnorm
functions.what: Frobenius norm of a square matrix.

functions.name: eig_random_sym
functions.what: Test helper: a symmetric `[n, n]` matrix with Park-Miller entries in $(-1, 1)$ from `seed`, so a failure can be quoted by its seed.

functions.name: eig_known_spectrum
functions.what: Test helper: Q diag(lam) Q^T for an orthogonal Q built from the vectors of a random matrix, so the spectrum is known exactly by construction (up to the rounding of the product).

functions.name: eig_agreement
functions.what: The worst member-to-member eigenvalue and projector gaps over the registry on one matrix, with k occupied vectors, and each member's worst residual and orthogonality defect.

functions.name: orth_threshold
functions.what: The threshold `orth_canon` uses: `opts[OPT_LINDEP]`, or `OPT_LINDEP_DEFAULT` when unset.

functions.name: orth_canon
functions.what: Member `ORTH_CANON`, the production one: canonical orthogonalization, columns with eigenvalue at or below the threshold dropped (kept columns first, in ascending order of their eigenvalue).

functions.name: orth_polish
functions.what: One Newton-Schulz step on the first m columns of X: X <- X (I - E/2) with E = X^T S X - I, so the new defect is of order E^2. The columns span the same space, so the SCF energy and density do not change. It matters when a kept eigenvalue of S is small, as on the diffuse H4 chain: the eigensolver's vectors are accurate only to about eps, and dividing by the square root of a small eigenvalue magnifies that error in X^T S X. E has to be formed with compensated sums (orth_gram_err) for the step to remove it [test "orth_canon drops exactly one vector on the diffuse H4 chain"].

functions.name: orth_prod_err
functions.what: The rounding error of p = fl(a b), so that a b = p + orth_prod_err(a, b, p) exactly (Dekker). The halves have at most half a double's significant bits, so every product of halves is exact and fusing one into an FMA changes nothing, which keeps the two engines in agreement.

functions.name: orth_gram_err
functions.what: E = X^T S X - I over the first m columns, as [m, m], each entry as accurate as a sum done in twice the working precision and then rounded. Every product carries its Dekker error and every addition its Knuth two-sum error. S x_b is kept as a hi + lo pair so the second product loses nothing either. Cost n^2 m + n m^2.

functions.name: orth_symm
functions.what: Member `ORTH_SYMM`: Lowdin's S^(-1/2).

functions.name: orth_cholesky
functions.what: The lower Cholesky factor L of S = L L^T.

functions.name: orth_chol
functions.what: Member `ORTH_CHOL`: X = L^(-T), by back substitution on L^T X = I.

functions.name: orth_sdot
functions.what: u^T S v for columns a of U and b of V.

functions.name: orth_gs
functions.what: Member `ORTH_GS`: Gram-Schmidt in the S inner product, two passes per vector.

functions.name: orth_methods
functions.what: The orthogonalizer registry, production member first.

functions.name: orth_rank
functions.what: Columns of X that are not all zero: the size m of the orthonormal space.

functions.name: orth_of
functions.what: The orthogonalizer `opts[OPT_ORTH]` names on S: `X[n, n]` with `X^T S X = I` over its first `orth_rank(X)` columns, the dropped columns zero. Each member is called by name, `orth_canon` (the production one) when the option is left at its default.

functions.name: orth_defect
functions.what: max |X^T S X - I| over the first m columns, formed with compensated sums so the measurement is not limited by its own rounding when X is large.

functions.name: orth_inverse_defect
functions.what: max |X X^T S - I|: X X^T is S^(-1) exactly when X has full rank.

functions.name: orth_check_all
functions.what: The worst X^T S X defect over the registry, and how many members did not keep exactly `mwant` columns, for one overlap matrix.

functions.name: den_stack1
functions.what: A `[1, n, n]` stack holding one matrix.

functions.name: den_stack2
functions.what: A `[2, n, n]` stack holding two matrices.

functions.name: den_from_vectors
functions.what: `w sum_(k = k0 .. k1-1) (X V[:, k]) (X V[:, k])^T`, `[n, n]`, with `X[n, m]` (its first m columns) and the eigenvectors `V[m, m]` as columns.

functions.name: den_fock
functions.what: The Fock matrices from J and K, `[nd, n, n]`: `H + J - K/2` for one total density, `H + J_a + J_b - K_s` for two spin densities.

functions.name: den_orth
functions.what: `X^T A X` over the first m columns of X: a matrix in the orthonormal basis.

functions.name: den_orth_density
functions.what: `X^T S D S X`: the density D in the orthonormal basis.

functions.name: den_orth_density_sx
functions.what: `U^T D U` with `U = S X` computed once: the density D in the orthonormal basis, for a loop that moves a new density there every iteration.

functions.name: den_commutator
functions.what: `F' P' - P' F'` for two `[m, m]` matrices: the SCF error in the orthonormal basis.

functions.name: den_commutator_sym
functions.what: `F' P' - P' F'` for two symmetric `[m, m]` matrices, as `A - A^T` with `A = F' P'`: one matrix product instead of two, since `(F' P')^T = P' F'` when both are symmetric. The result is antisymmetric to the bit. `den_commutator` is the definition term by term, and the test below holds the two together.

functions.name: den_maxabs
functions.what: The largest |entry| of a matrix.

functions.name: den_ao_commutator
functions.what: max |F D S - S D F| in the AO basis, for density d and Fock matrix f.

functions.name: den_trace
functions.what: Tr(D[d] S).

functions.name: den_trace2
functions.what: Tr(D[a] S D[b] S).

functions.name: den_idempotency
functions.what: max |D S D - w D| for density d.

functions.name: den_fnorm
functions.what: Frobenius norm of D[d].

functions.name: den_gap
functions.what: max |A[a] - B[b]| over two stacks of matrices.

functions.name: den_energy
functions.what: `E_nuc + (1/2) sum_d Tr(D_d (H + F_d))` over `ndens` densities.

functions.name: den_s2
functions.what: `<S^2>` of a UHF pair of spin densities D[0] (alpha), D[1] (beta).

functions.name: den_lowest
functions.what: Indices of the `k` smallest entries of `v`, ascending by value; entries whose `mask` is `1` are skipped. Ties go to the lower index.

functions.name: int_jk_is_direct
functions.what: `1` when J/K member `k` is one of the direct ones, which read a basis blob in place of packed integrals.

functions.name: int_basis_blob
functions.what: The basis blob that the direct members read (layout in the header). `M` is the c2s matrix for a spherical basis; pass `spherical = 0` for Cartesian, and then `M` is not read. The Schwarz factors of the shell pairs are computed here, once.

functions.name: int_blob_pack
functions.what: One `[rows, cols]` pack read back out of a blob, starting at `k0`.

functions.name: int_blob_basis
functions.what: The basis a blob holds, as a record (see the header for the layout).

functions.name: int_dens_cart
functions.what: The densities `D[nd, n, n]` in the Cartesian functions the integrals are computed in: `M D M^T` for a spherical basis, `D` as it is otherwise.

functions.name: int_jk_run
functions.what: Cartesian J and K `R[2 nd, nc, nc]` in the run's functions: `M^T R M` for a spherical basis, `R` as it is otherwise.

functions.name: int_jk_direct
functions.what: J/K member `INT_JK_DIRECT`, the production one: direct J and K from the basis blob in `X2`, screened by the Schwarz bound and the density, on the generated kernels in the run's functions (lib/hf/mdg_eri). `X1` and `X3` are not read.

functions.name: int_jk_direct_full
functions.what: J/K member `INT_JK_DIRECT_FULL`: direct J and K from the basis blob in `X2`, every quartet the Schwarz test keeps. `X1` and `X3` are not read.

functions.name: jk_packed
functions.what: Member `JK_PACKED`, the production one: one pass over the packed vector.

functions.name: jk_pairs
functions.what: Member `JK_PAIRS`: the integrals as a pair matrix.

functions.name: jk_dense
functions.what: Member `JK_DENSE`: the dense tensor and the definitions as written.

functions.name: jk_methods
functions.what: The J/K registry, production member first.

functions.name: jk_of
functions.what: J and K of the densities `D[ndens, n, n]`, `[2 ndens, n, n]`, by the member `opts[OPT_JK]` names: `jk_packed` (the production member), `jk_pairs`, `jk_dense`, or `int_jk_direct`, which reads the basis blob in `Gp`.

functions.name: jk_update
functions.what: J and K of the densities `D` from those of the densities `Dlast` they were last built from: `JKlast + JK(D - Dlast)`. J and K are linear in the density, so this is the whole build up to rounding and to what screening drops, and the direct member's density screening (lib/hf/md_direct) skips most quartets of a small change. The incremental Fock build of the SCF loop (lib/hf/scf_loop) calls it by name; PySCF's direct SCF builds its potential from `dm - dm_last` the same way (`get_veff`).

functions.name: jk_rebuild
functions.what: J and K of the densities `D` from the whole density, the last build unused: what `jk_update` is held to.

functions.name: jk_build_methods
functions.what: The ways to build the next J and K, the incremental one first.

functions.name: jk_t_opts
functions.what: The options array with J/K member `k` and the defaults.

functions.name: jk_rhf_energy
functions.what: The RHF energy of a reference total density, with J/K from member k: E_nuc + (1/2) Tr D (2H + J - K/2).

functions.name: jk_uhf_energy
functions.what: The UHF energy of reference spin densities, with J/K from member k.

functions.name: accel_capacity
functions.what: The ring capacity: opts[OPT_DIIS_N], at least `1`.

functions.name: accel_meta_new
functions.what: A fresh meta vector for a ring of capacity `nd`.

functions.name: accel_new
functions.what: An empty history for `k` matrices of `m x m` a step.

functions.name: accel_slot
functions.what: The ring slot holding the step `age` steps before the newest (age `0`).

functions.name: accel_push
functions.what: Store the newest Fock matrix `Fp[k, m, m]` and its error `Ep` in the ring. Returns the number of steps stored.

functions.name: accel_inner
functions.what: `<E, hist[slot]>` for an error `E` of the history's shape `[k, m, m]`: the one inner product the DIIS matrix is made of, so the kept and the recomputed `gram` agree to the bit. It is the `sum` of the elementwise product, not `dot` of the flattened arrays: in wasm `ravel` and `dot` go through the runtime bridge and cost more than the product itself (study/ports/pyscf FRICTION pyscf-022).

functions.name: accel_gram
functions.what: The inner products of every stored error pair, `[nd, nd]` by ring slot, recomputed from the history: what `accel_push` keeps in `gram`.

functions.name: accel_newest
functions.what: The newest Fock matrix, as a fresh `[ndens, m, m]` array.

functions.name: accel_solve
functions.what: Solve the k x k system A x = y in place by Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting; x overwrites y. Returns `1`, or `0` when a pivot is below `tol` times the largest entry of A (the system is then treated as singular and y is left unusable).

functions.name: accel_diis_coeffs
functions.what: DIIS coefficients over the newest `k` stored steps, from the inner products `G` of the stored errors (by ring slot): `1`, or `0` when the system is singular, and the coefficients `c[0..k-1]` (`c[t]` belongs to the step of age t).

functions.name: accel_cdiis_gram
functions.what: Commutator DIIS from the history and the inner products `G` of its errors. When the full history is singular it drops the oldest steps until the system solves; with one step it is plain iteration.

functions.name: accel_cdiis
functions.what: Member `ACCEL_CDIIS`, the production one: commutator DIIS, with the inner products recomputed from the history (`accel_extrapolate` passes the ones `accel_push` kept instead).

functions.name: accel_none
functions.what: Member `ACCEL_NONE`: plain iteration.

functions.name: accel_damp
functions.what: Member `ACCEL_DAMP`: damping against the matrix the previous step used.

functions.name: accel_methods
functions.what: The accelerator registry, production member first.

functions.name: accel_extrapolate
functions.what: The matrix the accelerator `opts[OPT_ACCEL]` names makes of the history, `[k, m, m]`; it is also recorded in slot `2 nd` as the matrix this step used. Each member is called by name, `accel_cdiis` (the production one) when the option is left at its default.

functions.name: accel_t_opts
functions.what: The options array with accelerator `k`, DIIS size `n` and the defaults.

functions.name: accel_t_system
functions.what: The matrix of the test problem, one row and column per unknown.

functions.name: accel_t_residual
functions.what: residual y - A x of the flattened x[0, :, :] into e[0, :, :]; returns its largest entry.

functions.name: accel_t_run
functions.what: Run `steps` Richardson steps under accelerator k; returns the final residual.

functions.name: gs_eig
functions.what: The eigen-decomposition of `X^T A X` (m columns of X kept) by eigensolver `opts[OPT_EIGEN]`: a member result, `[m + 1, m]` (lib/hf/eigen).

functions.name: gs_spins
functions.what: Spin densities `[2, n, n]` from the lowest `na` and `nb` eigenvectors in V.

functions.name: gs_occupy
functions.what: Occupy the lowest `na` and `nb` eigenvectors of `X^T A X` as spin densities.

functions.name: gs_fractional
functions.what: Occupation numbers for `N` electrons over the ascending levels `vals`: two per orbital from the bottom, and the electrons left for the partly filled level shared equally by every orbital within GS_AVG_DEGEN of it. Returns them and the number of orbitals with `f > 0`.

functions.name: gs_frac_density
functions.what: The total density `sum f_k c_k c_k^T` over the first `nocc` orbitals.

functions.name: gs_avg
functions.what: Member `GS_AVG`, the production one: the spin-averaged SCF, then aufbau per spin.

functions.name: gs_core
functions.what: Member `GS_CORE`: diagonalize the core Hamiltonian.

functions.name: gs_gwh_matrix
functions.what: The generalized Wolfsberg-Helmholz matrix.

functions.name: gs_gwh
functions.what: Member `GS_GWH`: generalized Wolfsberg-Helmholz.

functions.name: gs_zero
functions.what: Member `GS_ZERO`: nothing.

functions.name: gs_import
functions.what: Member `GS_IMPORT`: the caller's densities.

functions.name: gs_methods
functions.what: The guess registry, production member first.

functions.name: gs_of
functions.what: The starting spin densities `[2, n, n]` of the guess `opts[OPT_GUESS]` names. `D0` is what `gs_import` hands back. Each member is called by name, `gs_avg` (the production one) when the option is left at its default.

functions.name: rohf_feff
functions.what: The effective matrix `sum_xy Q_x (a_xy F_a + b_xy F_b) Q_y` over the closed, open and virtual projectors, `[1, m, m]`.

functions.name: rohf_c_gs
functions.what: Member 0: Guest-Saunders, PySCF's coupling.

functions.name: rohf_c_roothaan
functions.what: Member 1: Roothaan.

functions.name: rohf_c_mcweeny
functions.what: Member 2: McWeeny-Diercksen.

functions.name: rohf_c_bpd
functions.what: Member 3: Binkley-Pople-Dobosh.

functions.name: rohf_couplings
functions.what: The coupling registry, PySCF's first.

functions.name: rohf_effective
functions.what: The effective matrix `[1, m, m]` of coupling `opts[OPT_ROHF_COUPLING]`.

functions.name: rohf_error
functions.what: The ROHF error `Fe (P_c + P_o/2) - (P_c + P_o/2) Fe`, `[1, m, m]`, by the one-product commutator of lib/hf/density: the effective matrix is symmetrized when it is made and both projectors are symmetric.

functions.name: rohf_pick
functions.what: Which of the orbitals `V[m, m]` (columns) are closed and which open: `[2, m]`, row 0 the `nb` closed ones (lowest in `(F_a + F_b)/2`, ascending), row 1 the `na - nb` open ones (lowest in `F_a` among the rest).

functions.name: rohf_occupy
functions.what: The ROHF spin densities `[2, n, n]` of the orbitals `X V`: each closed orbital once in both, each open one once in `Da`, in the order picked.

functions.name: rohf_occupations
functions.what: The occupation of each orbital, `[m]`: 2 closed, 1 open, 0 virtual.

functions.name: rohf_level_shift
functions.what: The effective matrix `Fu[1, m, m]` with its virtual block raised by `shift`: `Fu + shift (I - P_c - P_o)`.

functions.name: scf_setup
functions.what: A setup from the matrices, the electron counts, the nuclear repulsion and the options.

functions.name: scf_setup_with
functions.what: The same setup with options `o`, its method decided again from them. A record update that changes the options' method or the electron counts would keep the old method; this and `scf_setup` are the ways to change them.

functions.name: scf_method
functions.what: The method options `o` ask for with `na` alpha and `nb` beta electrons: `o.method`, where automatic means RHF for equal spin counts and UHF otherwise. `scf_setup` asks it once and stores the answer in the setup.

functions.name: scf_opts
functions.what: The column array the registry members read (lib/hf/opts).

functions.name: scf_weight
functions.what: Electrons per orbital: two for the RHF total density, one for a spin density.

functions.name: scf_nocc
functions.what: The orbitals density d fills: `nalpha` for RHF and for alpha, `nbeta` for beta.

functions.name: scf_incremental
functions.what: The full-rebuild interval of the incremental Fock build: `fock_rebuild` when the run builds J and K with the production direct member, `0` (every build from the whole density) otherwise. In core a build costs the same whatever the density, so only the direct member gains from it.

functions.name: scf_nmatrix
functions.what: How many matrices DIIS extrapolates: one per density for RHF and UHF, the one effective matrix for ROHF.

functions.name: scf_swapped
functions.what: The same setup with the spin counts exchanged.

functions.name: scf_energy2
functions.what: The energy a second way, from J and K directly instead of from the Fock matrix: `E_nuc + Tr D H + (1/2) Tr D J - (1/4) Tr D K` for one total density, `E_nuc + Tr Dt H + (1/2) Tr Dt Jt - (1/2) sum_s Tr D_s K_s` for two.

functions.name: scf_commutator
functions.what: The Fock matrices and densities in the orthonormal basis of `X` (its `m` columns), the matrix DIIS extrapolates and its error. `U` is `S X`, which the loop computes once.

functions.name: scf_level_shift
functions.what: `Fnext` (the matrices about to be diagonalized, `[k, m, m]`) with the virtual orbitals raised by `shift`: `Fnext + shift (I - P'/w)` per spin for RHF and UHF, where `P'/w` projects on the occupied orbitals, and `Fnext + shift (I - P_c' - P_o')` for ROHF.

functions.name: scf_diagonalize
functions.what: The eigen-decomposition of each matrix of `Fnext`: a stack of eigensolver results, `[k, m + 1, m]` (lib/hf/eigen).

functions.name: scf_occupy
functions.what: The next densities from the eigenvectors in `eigs`: the lowest orbitals of each density for RHF and UHF, the closed and open ones for ROHF.

functions.name: scf_iterate
functions.what: The loop: iterate from the densities `D0` (`[1, n, n]` for RHF, `[2, n, n]` otherwise) until the energy and the commutator settle, or `max_iter` iterations have run.

functions.name: scf_coefficients
functions.what: `X V`: orbitals as AO coefficients, `[n, m]`.

functions.name: scf_aufbau
functions.what: The aufbau occupations of `m` orbitals with `nocc` filled, `w` each.

functions.name: scf_orbitals
functions.what: The orbitals of one Fock matrix `Fd[n, n]`: its eigenvectors in the orthonormal basis of `X`, the lowest `nocc` filled with `w` electrons each.

functions.name: scf_result
functions.what: The result record of a run that ended with densities D, Fock matrices F (and their J and K) built from the densities before them, energy e, convergence flag `conv` and `it` iterations.

functions.name: scf_unswap
functions.what: The same result with the two spins exchanged.

functions.name: scf_solve
functions.what: The one way into the loop: iterate from spin densities `start[2, n, n]` (in the setup's spin order) with the method the setup asks for.

functions.name: scf
functions.what: The SCF of a setup: from the guess `setup.options.guess`, the method the setup asks for, iterated until it converges.

functions.name: scf_run_from
functions.what: From the spin densities `Da` and `Db` (for RHF, any split of the total density, such as half of it each).

functions.name: scf_step
functions.what: One plain step from `Da`, `Db`: build F, diagonalize, occupy, with no extrapolation and no level shift. The result's energy and Fock matrices are those of the densities given; its densities are the new ones.

functions.name: scf_densities
functions.what: The spin densities of a result as the `[nd, n, n]` stack the loop carries: the total density for RHF, alpha then beta otherwise.

functions.name: scf_density_gap
functions.what: The largest difference between two results' densities: the total density for RHF, spin by spin otherwise.

functions.name: scf_t_model
functions.what: Test helper: PySCF's atom-free model (test_rhf.py:757, test_uhf.py:374): a diagonal h, S = I, one on-site integral (ii|ii) per orbital, no nuclei.

functions.name: scf_blob
functions.what: The basis blob the direct J/K member reads (lib/hf/jk_direct).

functions.name: scf_run_options
functions.what: The options a run uses: a direct run starts from the core Hamiltonian when it asks for the averaged guess, which needs packed integrals.

functions.name: scf_setup_of
functions.what: A setup from integrals computed elsewhere: the molecule gives the electron counts and the nuclear repulsion.

functions.name: integrals
functions.what: The setup of a run on molecule `mol` with options `o`: its integrals, each by its production member, its electron counts and its nuclear repulsion. A direct run (`o.jk = INT_JK_DIRECT` or `INT_JK_DIRECT_FULL`) gets the basis blob in place of the packed integrals.

functions.name: scf_with
functions.what: Hartree-Fock with options `o`.

functions.name: rhf
functions.what: Restricted Hartree-Fock with the production options.

functions.name: uhf
functions.what: Unrestricted Hartree-Fock with the production options.

functions.name: rohf
functions.what: Restricted open-shell Hartree-Fock with the production options.

functions.name: sw_rep_new
functions.what: A fresh report vector.

functions.name: sw_flat_index
functions.what: The flat indices `0 .. N-1`, for `take` and `put`.

functions.name: sw_table_median
functions.what: Elementwise median of the rows of `T` (`nstrat` by `N`) into `C`, over the first `ncmp` columns; later columns copy row `0` and are never compared. Returns the worst relative deviation and records the member and flat index that produced it in `rep`. With an even count the upper middle value is the median, the same choice `sweep` in lang/viv/std/contracts.viv makes.

functions.name: sw_rep_release
functions.what: The report a release run leaves: member `0` ran alone, nothing was compared.

functions.name: sw_verdict
functions.what: `1` when the report's worst deviation is under `tol`, else `0`.

functions.name: sw_run3_arr
functions.what: Run the registry (or member `0` alone when `release` is `1`) and return the consensus in the members' shape. Every member gets its own copy of the inputs, so one that writes into an input cannot corrupt the next.

functions.name: sweep3_arr
functions.what: Debug: run every member, assert agreement to `tol`, return the consensus. Release: return member 0's result.

functions.name: sw_check3_arr
functions.what: Like `sweep3_arr` without the assertion: the consensus goes into `out` (any array with `N` entries) and the return value is the verdict.

functions.name: sw_check3_num
functions.what: The consensus goes into `out[0]`; the return value is the verdict.

functions.name: sw_cov_new
functions.what: A `[nclass, SW_COV_NSTRAT]` table of hit counts, one column per strategy.

functions.name: sw_cov_hit
functions.what: Count one check of class `cls` by strategy `strat` (below SW_COV_NSTRAT).

functions.name: sw_cov_nstrat
functions.what: Distinct strategies that have checked class `cls`.

functions.name: sw_cov_covered
functions.what: Classes that at least one strategy has checked.

functions.name: sw_cov_min_strat
functions.what: The fewest strategies behind any covered class; `0` when nothing is covered.

functions.name: sw_cov_gate
functions.what: The build gate: every covered class was checked by at least two strategies.

functions.name: sw_cov_report
functions.what: One line per covered class: [class, strategies, total hits].

functions.name: sw_cls_eri
functions.what: The ERI class of (la lb|lc ld), canonical under the 8-fold symmetry: the larger l first within each pair, then the larger pair first. `l <= 4`.

functions.name: sw_cls_boys
functions.what: The Boys class of order `n <= 16` at argument `x`: `SW_NXBIN` x-bins with edges `0.1, 1, 5, 15, 30, 50, 100`.

functions.name: sw_t_tensor
functions.what: A `SW_T_DIM^4` tensor with entry `[1,0,1,0] = 2`, standing in for an ERI block.

functions.name: sw_t_good2
functions.what: The same tensor, filled in the opposite loop order.

functions.name: sw_t_bad
functions.what: The planted bug: one entry off by `1e-9`.

functions.name: sw_t_tailbad
functions.what: Wrong only in the last entry, flat index `SW_T_LEN - 1`, which a window of `SW_T_LEN - 1` entries excludes.

functions.name: sw_t_never
functions.what: A member that must never run: it fails the enclosing test if it does.

functions.name: sw_t_clobber
functions.what: A member that writes into its first input.

functions.name: sw_t_jk
functions.what: J/K-shaped members: `(X1, X2, X3, D, opts) -> [2, n, n]` with `J = 2D`, `K = D`.

functions.name: sw_t_sum
functions.what: Scalar members: the sum of a's entries three ways.

functions.name: sw_t_powrec
functions.what: (nmax, x) members: x^k / k! for k = 0..nmax, by recurrence and by pow.

functions.name: os_ncum
functions.what: Components with total power below `l`.

functions.name: os_cidx
functions.what: Index of component (lx, ly, lz) in the table of `os_ctab`.

functions.name: os_ctab
functions.what: One row per Cartesian component with total power up to `L`: the powers, `l`, the index one step down along x, y, z (-1 where that power is 0), one step up (-1 at `l = L`), and the pivot, the first axis with a nonzero power (-1 for s). The recurrences lower the pivot.

functions.name: os_s1d
functions.what: The 1-D overlap table `S[i, j]`, `i <= la`, `j <= lb`, for exponents `a` and `b` on centers `A` and `B` along one axis. The table is written into `S` (at least `[la+1, lb+1]`).

functions.name: os_t1d
functions.what: The 1-D kinetic table `T[i, j]` from the overlap table `S` of the same pair (filled by `os_s1d`). Written into `T`.

functions.name: os_st_block
functions.what: Overlap (`kind` 0) or kinetic (`kind` 1) block of shells `sa`, `sb`, `[ncart(la), ncart(lb)]`, unit-Cartesian.

functions.name: os_overlap_block
functions.what: Overlap block of shells `sa`, `sb`.

functions.name: os_kinetic_block
functions.what: Kinetic block of shells `sa`, `sb`.

functions.name: os_nuclear_block
functions.what: Nuclear attraction block of shells `sa`, `sb`: `-sum_C Z_C <a|1/r_C|b>` over every row of `atoms`. The vertical recurrence builds `Theta(e)^(m)` for every `e` up to `la + lb` on A; primitives and nuclei are summed into `acc[e]` for `la <= l_e <= la + lb`, and the horizontal step then moves `lb` units of power to B.

functions.name: os_hrr_pair
functions.what: The horizontal step on a one-electron pair: from `acc[e]` (every `e` with `la <= l_e <= la + lb`, on A) to the block `[ncart(la), ncart(lb)]`, times the component factors. `(a, b+1_i) = (a+1_i, b) + AB_i (a, b)`.

functions.name: os_matrix
functions.what: Fill a whole matrix from per-pair blocks: `kind` 0 overlap, 1 kinetic, 2 nuclear attraction. Only `sa >= sb` is computed; the other triangle is the transpose.

functions.name: os_overlap
functions.what: Stage member: the overlap matrix, `[nao_cart, nao_cart]`.

functions.name: os_kinetic
functions.what: Stage member: the kinetic energy matrix.

functions.name: os_nuclear
functions.what: Stage member: the nuclear attraction matrix, over every atom's charge.

functions.name: gh_count_below
functions.what: How many nodes of the `n`-point rule lie below `t`: the number of negative pivots of the LDL^T factorization of `J - t I`, where `J` is the Jacobi matrix (zero diagonal, off-diagonal `sqrt(k/2)` between rows `k - 1` and `k`). Sylvester's law of inertia makes it the count of eigenvalues below `t`.

functions.name: gh_orthonormal
functions.what: The orthonormal Hermite polynomial `p_n(t)` for weight `exp(-t^2)` and its derivative, by the three-term recurrence `sqrt(k + 1) p_(k+1) = sqrt(2) t p_k - sqrt(k) p_(k-1)`, `p_0 = pi^(-1/4)`, differentiated term by term, and the sum of `p_k(t)^2` for `k < n`.

functions.name: gh_rule
functions.what: The `n`-point Gauss-Hermite rule for weight `exp(-t^2)`: `R[0, k]` is a node, `R[1, k]` its weight, nodes in decreasing order. The nodes are the eigenvalues of the Jacobi matrix (Golub and Welsch). Node `k`, counting down from the largest, is where `gh_count_below` steps from `n - 1 - k` to `n - k`: `GH_BISECT_IT` halvings of the Gershgorin interval `|t| <= sqrt(2n) + 1` find it, then up to `GH_NEWTON_IT` Newton steps on `p_n` polish it. Its weight is the Christoffel number `1 / sum_(j < n) p_j(t)^2` (Gautschi). Only the nonnegative half is computed; the rule is symmetric.

functions.name: gh_axis
functions.what: The 1-D overlap and kinetic tables for one primitive pair along one axis, `S[i, j]` and `T[i, j]` for `i <= la`, `j <= lb`, by quadrature with rule `R`. `U` is scratch, `[2, lmax + 2]` at least.

functions.name: gh_block
functions.what: Overlap (`kind` 0) or kinetic (`kind` 1) block of shells `sa`, `sb`, `[ncart(la), ncart(lb)]`, unit-Cartesian, with rule `R`.

functions.name: gh_rule_for
functions.what: The rule that is exact for every kinetic integrand of a shell pack: degree `2 lmax + 2` needs `lmax + 2` nodes.

functions.name: gh_matrix
functions.what: A whole matrix from per-pair blocks, `sa >= sb` computed and mirrored.

functions.name: gh_overlap
functions.what: Stage member: the overlap matrix, `[nao_cart, nao_cart]`.

functions.name: gh_kinetic
functions.what: Stage member: the kinetic energy matrix.

functions.name: gh_t_moment_err
functions.what: Test helper: the largest relative error of the `n`-point rule over the moments `int t^k exp(-t^2) dt` for `k <= 2n - 1`: 0 for odd `k`, and `(k-1)!! / 2^(k/2) sqrt(pi)` for even `k`. An odd moment is measured against `sum w |t|^k`, the size of the terms that cancel in it.

functions.name: hgp_ncum
functions.what: Components with total power below `l`.

functions.name: hgp_cidx
functions.what: Index of component (lx, ly, lz) in the table of `hgp_ctab`.

functions.name: hgp_ctab
functions.what: One row per Cartesian component with total power up to `L`: the powers, `l`, the index one step down along x, y, z (-1 where that power is 0), one step up (-1 at `l = L`), and the pivot, the first axis with a nonzero power (-1 for s). Both recurrences lower the pivot.

functions.name: hgp_vrr
functions.what: The vertical recurrence for one primitive quartet, written into `V[e, f, m]`, then added into `acc[e - ncum(la), f - ncum(lc)]` for `la <= l_e <= La` and `lc <= l_f <= Lc`. `g` holds the quartet's geometry: PA, WP, QC, WQ (3 each, from index 0), then 1/(2 zeta), rho/zeta, 1/(2 eta), rho/eta, 1/(2(zeta + eta)), the prefactor and rho PQ^2 (from index 12).

functions.name: hgp_quartet
functions.what: The unit-Cartesian block `[ncart(la), ncart(lb), ncart(lc), ncart(ld)]` of shells `sa`, `sb`, `sc`, `sd`, in that order. `CT` must reach `la + lb + 1` and `lc + ld + 1`.

functions.name: hgp_hrr
functions.what: Both horizontal steps on the contracted `acc[e, f]` (bra power all on A, ket power all on C), then the component factors.

functions.name: hgp_ctab_for
functions.what: The component table big enough for every quartet of a shell pack.

functions.name: hgp_min_exp
functions.what: The smallest exponent of shell `s`.

functions.name: hgp_swap
functions.what: `true` when shell `t` should go first in the pair (s, t), `false` when `s` should.  The vertical step puts all of a pair's power on its first center, and the horizontal step moves some of it to the second. The higher `l` goes first, so there is less to move. Between equal `l`, the shell with the larger smallest exponent goes first: the product Gaussian sits near the tighter center, so powers of the distance to it stay small, while powers of the distance to the diffuse center grow and then cancel in the horizontal step. On the prims (ff|ff) set, ordering by `l` alone leaves errors of 8.8e-12 relative to the exact value, and 1.2e-10 on one Schwarz diagonal; with the exponent tie-break the worst are 2.1e-13 and 1.4e-13 (measured against an mpmath HGP at 40 digits). Ordering every pair by exponent alone gave the same worst errors and took 7% longer on water def2-TZVP.

functions.name: hgp_block
functions.what: The block of shells (s1 s2|s3 s4) in that index order, computed in the order `hgp_swap` picks for each pair.

functions.name: hgp_store
functions.what: One shell quartet into the packed vector. Packed-8 indices do not depend on the order of the indices, so the block goes in as `hgp_quartet` returns it, in whatever order `hgp_swap` chose.

functions.name: hgp_eri
functions.what: Stage member: every unique (ij|kl) of the basis, packed-8, `[es_len8(nao_cart)]`, unit-Cartesian, unscreened.

functions.name: rys_applicable
functions.what: 1 when Rys is validated for total angular momentum `ltot` (a quartet's la + lb + lc + ld), else 0.

functions.name: rys_nroot
functions.what: Roots needed for total angular momentum `ltot`.

functions.name: rys_gl_half
functions.what: The positive half of the `2m`-point Gauss-Legendre rule: `GL[0, i]` is a node in (0, 1) and `GL[1, i]` its weight. The rule is symmetric, so for an even integrand the half with these weights gives the integral over [0, 1]. Newton on `P_2m` from the cosine guess converges quadratically; 12 steps is past the point where the nodes stop moving.

functions.name: rys_work_new
functions.what: Workspace for `rys_roots`: rows 0-1 are the folded Gauss-Legendre rule, rows 2-5 hold the discrete measure (u, mass) and the last two orthogonal polynomials at its nodes. Allocate once per integral build.

functions.name: rys_hypot
functions.what: sqrt(a^2 + b^2) without overflow or underflow in the squares.

functions.name: rys_tql
functions.what: Eigenvalues of the symmetric tridiagonal matrix with diagonal `J[0, 0..n-1]` and off-diagonal `J[1, 0..n-2]` by implicit QL with Wilkinson shifts: the `tql2` of EISPACK in the form the public-domain JAMA library gives it, as lib/hf/eigen's eig_tql2 has it. Only the first row of the eigenvector matrix is carried, in `J[2, ]`, because Golub-Welsch needs nothing else. On return `J[0, i]` is an eigenvalue and `J[2, i]` the first component of its unit eigenvector.

functions.name: rys_roots
functions.what: The `n`-point Rys rule for argument `x`: `R[0, i]` is a root `u_i = t_i^2` in (0, 1) and `R[1, i]` its weight, so that `sum_i R[1,i] R[0,i]^k = F_k(x)` for `k < 2n`. `W` is `rys_work_new()`; `J` is a `[3, RYS_NROOT_MAX]` scratch. Discretized Stieltjes gives the recurrence, Golub-Welsch the rule.

functions.name: rys_binom
functions.what: Binomial coefficient C(n, k) for small n.

functions.name: rys_shell_quartet
functions.what: The unit-Cartesian block of shell quartet (s1 s2|s3 s4), written into `blk` in the order ((ia*nb + ib)*nc + ic)*nd + id, components in PySCF's order. `cn` is `bas_contract(shells, prims)`; `W`, `J` and `R` are the scratch arrays of `rys_roots`. The per-quartet tables are allocated here, so they are freed when the quartet is done.

functions.name: rys_eri
functions.what: Registry member for the ERI stage: the packed-8 unit-Cartesian ERIs of a basis, every shell quartet by Rys quadrature. It computes every class; the classes it is validated for are those with `rys_applicable(la+lb+lc+ld)`.

functions.name: rys_rng
functions.what: Test helper: the next uniform number in (0, 1) from a Park-Miller state in `st[0]`, so a failing x can be quoted by its seed.

functions.name: rys_moment_gap
functions.what: Test helper: the worst relative gap between the `n`-point rule's moments `sum_i w_i u_i^k`, `k0 <= k < k1`, and `F` (the Boys values at the same x).

functions.name: rys_moment_worst
functions.what: Test helper: the worst moment gap over orders `k < 2n` at one x, with the Boys values from lib/hf/boys as the reference.

functions.name: rys_rule_ok
functions.what: Test helper: 1 when every root of the `n`-point rule at `x` lies in (0, 1) and every weight is positive, else 0.

functions.name: int_contract_closed
functions.what: Member `0`: the closed-form normalization of `lib/hf/basis`.

functions.name: int_prim_overlaps
functions.what: The overlap matrix of shell `s`'s primitives, each as its own normalized one-primitive shell at the origin, taken from overlap member `which` (`0` = md1_s, `1` = os_overlap). Entry `[p, q]` is the overlap of the `x^l` components, the first in PySCF's order.

functions.name: int_contract_by
functions.what: `cn` with each shell's self-overlap taken from integral member `which`.

functions.name: bas_contract_numeric
functions.what: Member `1`: self-overlaps from McMurchie-Davidson (`md1_s`).

functions.name: bas_contract_numeric_os
functions.what: Member `2`: self-overlaps from Obara-Saika (`os_overlap`).

functions.name: int_c2s_closed
functions.what: The c2s members take `(l, unused)` so they fit the `(nmax, x) -> Arr` driver; each returns M_l, `[ncart(l), nsph(l)]`.

functions.name: int_eri_sph_methods
functions.what: The spherical ERIs of a basis, production first: the generated kernels with spherical rows in the store (`mdg_sph`), md_eri's block-by-block transform (`mderi_sph`), and the Cartesian build followed by the ERI transform.

functions.name: int_jk_methods
functions.what: The J/K registry the pipeline passes to the SCF drivers: `lib/hf/jk`'s three in-core members, then the direct ones at `INT_JK_DIRECT` and `INT_JK_DIRECT_FULL`.

functions.name: int_mask_has
functions.what: `1` when member `k` is selected by `mask` (`0` selects every member).

functions.name: int_mask_count
functions.what: How many of the first `n` members `mask` selects, and the first of them (`-1` when none is).

functions.name: int_run3
functions.what: Run the members of `ms` that `mask` selects and return their consensus (elementwise median, `lib/hf/sweep`). With one member selected, or in release, only the first selected member runs. `rep[SW_REP_STRAT]` is the blamed member's index in `ms`.

functions.name: int_sweep3
functions.what: The asserting form: every selected member within `tol` of the consensus. When one member ran (release, or a one-member mask) nothing was compared and nothing is asserted.

functions.name: int_check3
functions.what: The non-asserting form: the consensus goes into `out`, the verdict (`1` agree, `0` dissent) is returned.

functions.name: int_run5
functions.what: `int_run3` for the J/K signature.

functions.name: int_contract
functions.what: The contracted coefficients `cn[nprimtot]`, every member within `INT_TOL_CN`.

functions.name: int_overlap
functions.what: The overlap matrix S, `[nao_cart, nao_cart]`, every member within `INT_TOL_ONE`.

functions.name: int_kinetic
functions.what: The kinetic-energy matrix T, every member within `INT_TOL_ONE`.

functions.name: int_nuclear
functions.what: The nuclear-attraction matrix V, every member within `INT_TOL_ONE`.

functions.name: int_eri
functions.what: The packed-8 unit-Cartesian ERIs from the members `mask` selects, within `INT_TOL_ERI`.

functions.name: int_c2s
functions.what: `M_l` for one shell of angular momentum `l`, both members within `INT_TOL_C2S`.

functions.name: int_sph2
functions.what: A one-electron matrix moved to spherical functions, `M^T X M`, within `INT_TOL_TR`.

functions.name: int_cart2
functions.what: One spherical density moved to Cartesian functions, `M D M^T`, within `INT_TOL_TR`.

functions.name: int_tr4_mask
functions.what: The ERI-transform mask: `tr4_quarter` unpacks to `[n,n,n,n]`, so it joins only while the Cartesian count is at most `INT_TR4_QUARTER_NMAX`.

functions.name: int_sph4
functions.what: Packed-8 spherical ERIs from packed-8 unit-Cartesian ones, within `INT_TOL_TR`.

functions.name: int_jk
functions.what: J and K, `[2 ndens, n, n]`, from densities `D[ndens, n, n]`, the members `mask` selects (bits `INT_JK_DIRECT` and `INT_JK_DIRECT_FULL`, the direct members, need `blob`), within `INT_TOL_JK`.

functions.name: int_anchor
functions.what: Never run: a call site for every def that takes a registry, so a program that uses this module without calling them still compiles.

functions.name: hf_eri_mask
functions.what: The ERI members the pipeline runs: the production one alone when the options turn cross-checking off, else `options.eri_members` (unset means MD and HGP).

functions.name: hf_one_mask
functions.what: The members the one-electron and transform stages run: every one, or the production one alone.

functions.name: hf_c2s
functions.what: The matrix that turns Cartesian basis functions into spherical ones.

functions.name: hf_to_ao
functions.what: A one-electron matrix in the run's functions: transformed to spherical ones when the molecule is spherical, as it is otherwise.

functions.name: hf_overlap
functions.what: The overlap matrix S: `ao_overlap`, or, with `cross_check` on, every member and their agreement.

functions.name: hf_hcore
functions.what: The core Hamiltonian `H = T + V`: `ao_hcore`, or, with `cross_check` on, every member and their agreement.

functions.name: hf_eri
functions.what: The electron repulsion integrals, packed-8, in the run's functions: `ao_eri`, or, with `cross_check` on, the members `hf_eri_mask` selects and their agreement.

functions.name: hf_blob
functions.what: The basis blob the direct J/K member reads (lib/hf/scf, `scf_blob`).

functions.name: hf_two_electron
functions.what: What the J/K stage reads: the packed integrals, or the basis blob for the direct member.

functions.name: hf_setup_of
functions.what: A setup from integrals computed elsewhere (lib/hf/scf, `scf_setup_of`).

functions.name: hf_setup
functions.what: A setup with every integral computed here: the production one of lib/hf/scf (`integrals`), or, with `cross_check` on, every integral member run and held to agree.

functions.name: hf_scf
functions.what: The SCF of a setup (lib/hf/scf_loop, `scf`).

functions.name: hf_scf_from
functions.what: The SCF from given spin densities.

functions.name: hf_step
functions.what: One plain SCF step from given spin densities (lib/hf/scf_loop, `scf_step`).

functions.name: hf_energy
functions.what: The whole pipeline: integrals, then the SCF.

functions.name: hf_electron_gap
functions.what: How far the densities are from holding their electrons: the largest `|Tr(D_d S) - N_d|`. The lock holds it at zero; lib/hf/scf_loop.debug holds each iteration's densities to the same.

functions.name: hf_lock_report
functions.what: Run the SCF of `p` and hold it to the reference energy `eref`.

functions.name: hf_lock_assert
functions.what: The lock contract: the RHF, UHF and ROHF rows of the contract table.

functions.name: hf_lock_full
functions.what: The full lock of a closed-shell molecule whose PySCF integrals are all stored: Cartesian integrals (members of `mask`) against PySCF's, the Cartesian RHF against `e6`, then the spherical transforms against PySCF's and the spherical RHF against `e5`. Returns the two energy gaps.

functions.name: hf_lock_sampled
functions.what: The lock of a closed-shell molecule whose PySCF integrals are sampled (checksums, the pair diagonal and seeded samples, Cartesian `ci..cs` and spherical `si..ss`), with the one-electron matrices in full. The Cartesian RHF runs when `cart` is set. Returns the two energy gaps (the first `0` when it does not).

functions.name: stretch_atoms
functions.what: The atoms with both hydrogens moved along their O-H bonds by the factor `s`; oxygen sits at the origin, so scaling a hydrogen's coordinates scales its bond and keeps the angle.

functions.name: stretch_energy
functions.what: The RHF energy of the molecule stretched by `s`, using only the default implementation of each step.

functions.name: ao_values
functions.what: The value of every basis function of `mol` at the point (x, y, z), in bohr. s and p shells only, in PySCF's order (p as x, y, z).

functions.name: ss_overlap
functions.what: The overlap of two s shells, by the Gaussian product theorem: an integral lib/hf computes its own way, so comparing the two checks that ao_values reads the tables and the contracted coefficients `cn` as lib/hf does.

functions.name: density_plane
functions.what: log10 of the electron density of D on the picture's grid, row 0 at the bottom.

posts.title: Hartree-Fock for water
posts.titleHtml: Hartree-Fock for water
posts.titleText: Hartree-Fock for water
posts.summaryHtml: Water in the STO-3G basis, from the basis to the restricted Hartree-Fock energy, using lib/hf, a library whose tests compare it against PySCF. The electron repulsion integrals are computed two independent ways, McMurchie-Davidson and Head-Gordon-Pople, which must agree; the energy matches PySCF 2.5.0 within 10−9 hartree.
posts.summaryText: Water in the STO-3G basis, from the basis to the restricted Hartree-Fock energy, using lib/hf, a library whose tests compare it against PySCF. The electron repulsion integrals are computed two independent ways, McMurchie-Davidson and Head-Gordon-Pople, which must agree; the energy matches PySCF 2.5.0 within 10^-9 hartree.
notes: The input is the molecule as PySCF takes it: the atoms as text, each an element symbol and its position in angstrom, and the basis set by its name, "sto-3g", found in a table generated from the Basis Set Exchange (lib/basis/sto3g). molecule (lib/hf/mole) turns them into the three tables lib/hf computes with: the atoms (charge and position in bohr), the shells of the basis (which atom, which angular momentum, where its primitives start) and the primitives (exponent and contraction coefficient). For water in STO-3G that is 3 atoms, 5 shells and 15 primitives, giving 7 basis functions, the same functions PySCF builds for the molecule.
Everything after that is computed by lib/hf, the same code whose tests compare it against PySCF on a set of molecules and basis sets (the reference values are in lib/hfref):

1. The overlap S, kinetic energy T and nuclear attraction V matrices. lib/hf has more than one implementation of each (three for S and T, two for V). Here every implementation runs, and the program stops if any two disagree by more than 10−12. 2. The electron repulsion integrals (μν∣λσ), 406 of them once the eightfold permutation symmetry is used. Two independent methods compute them: McMurchie-Davidson, which expands each product of Gaussians in Hermite Gaussians, and Head-Gordon-Pople, which runs the Obara-Saika vertical recurrence and then the horizontal one. They share no recurrence. The program compares them entry by entry and stops if any integral differs by more than 10−12 relative, naming the method and the integral. 3. The self-consistent field, using only the default implementation of each step: a starting guess from a spin-averaged calculation, DIIS acceleration (which combines the Fock matrices of the last few iterations to make the commutator FDS−SDF as small as possible), canonical orthogonalization, and the Coulomb and exchange matrices J and K from the packed integrals. It solves F(D)C=SCε repeatedly until the change in energy and the commutator both fall below their tolerances, and E is the formula above.
The energy matches PySCF's −74.9630631297292 within 10−9.

The figure moves the two hydrogens along their O-H bonds, keeping the angle, and reruns the whole calculation at five more bond lengths, using only the default implementations. Each energy is checked against PySCF at the same geometry. A parabola through the three points around the stored geometry puts the bottom at 0.987 angstrom. PySCF's own minimization along the same line gives 0.98704. The stored geometry has O-H at 0.958 angstrom, close to the experimental bond length, so STO-3G makes the bond about 3 percent too long.
posts.equationHtml: E=Enuc​+21​μν∑​Dνμ​(Hμν​+Fμν​)
posts.source:
from hf.mole import molecule
from hf.molecule import Molecule
from hf.basis import bas_contract, AT_X, AT_Y, AT_Z, SH_ATOM, SH_L, SH_NPRIM, SH_P0, SH_CART0, PR_EXP
from hf.scf import rhf
from hf.opts import scf_checked, scf_defaults
from hf.hf import hf_hcore, hf_overlap, hf_scf, hf_setup_of, hf_step
from hf.integrals import int_eri, INT_ERI_PAIR
from hf.sweep import sw_rep_new, SW_REP_NSTRAT, SW_REP_WORST, sw_verdict

# PySCF's conversion from bohr to angstrom (pyscf.lib.param.BOHR).
BOHR_ANGSTROM = 0.52917721092

# water as tools/hf_reference.py gives it to PySCF
water = molecule("O 0 0 0; H 0 -0.757 0.587; H 0 0.757 0.587", "sto-3g")

# ---- the cross-checked build: every one-electron implementation, both integral methods
checked = scf_checked()
S_water = hf_overlap(water, checked)
H_water = hf_hcore(water, checked)
eri_report = sw_rep_new()
G_water = int_eri(water.atoms, water.shells, water.prims, INT_ERI_PAIR, eri_report)

# ---- the SCF, using only the default implementation of each step
water_result = hf_scf(hf_setup_of(water, H_water, S_water, G_water, scf_defaults()))
E_water = water_result.energy

# The worst gap itself sits at rounding level and its last digits depend on
# the platform's exp, so the post shows the verdict and asserts the bound.
eri_families_swept = eri_report[SW_REP_NSTRAT]
mcmurchie_davidson_and_head_gordon_pople_agree_to_1e_12 = sw_verdict(eri_report, 1.0e-12)
show E_water
say("integral methods cross-checked", eri_families_swept)
say("McMurchie-Davidson and Head-Gordon-Pople agree within 1e-12 (1 = yes)", mcmurchie_davidson_and_head_gordon_pople_agree_to_1e_12)

# ---- the symmetric stretch, using only the default implementation of each step
#| The atoms with both hydrogens moved along their O-H bonds by the factor
#| `s`; oxygen sits at the origin, so scaling a hydrogen's coordinates scales
#| its bond and keeps the angle.
def stretch_atoms(atoms: Arr, s) {
    a = atoms + 0.0
    for k to 2 {
        a[k + 1, AT_X] = atoms[k + 1, AT_X] * s
        a[k + 1, AT_Y] = atoms[k + 1, AT_Y] * s
        a[k + 1, AT_Z] = atoms[k + 1, AT_Z] * s
    }
    return a
}

#| The RHF energy of the molecule stretched by `s`, using only the default
#| implementation of each step.
def stretch_energy(mol: Molecule, s) {
    r = rhf(Molecule { atoms: stretch_atoms(mol.atoms, s), ..mol })
    return r.energy
}

STRETCH = [0.85, 0.95, 1.0, 1.05, 1.15, 1.3]
# PySCF 2.5.0 RHF/STO-3G at the same stretched geometries (conv_tol 1e-12)
STRETCH_PYSCF = [-74.87015730235669, -74.94969700178768, -74.9630631297292, -74.96430257205597, -74.94124852220563, -74.8695743402323]

r_water_bohr = sqrt(water.atoms[1, AT_Y] * water.atoms[1, AT_Y] + water.atoms[1, AT_Z] * water.atoms[1, AT_Z])
stretch_E = zeros(len(STRETCH))
stretch_r = zeros(len(STRETCH))
for k to len(STRETCH) {
    stretch_r[k] = r_water_bohr * STRETCH[k] * BOHR_ANGSTROM
    if STRETCH[k] == 1.0 {
        stretch_E[k] = E_water
    }
    else {
        stretch_E[k] = stretch_energy(water, STRETCH[k])
    }
}

# The bottom of the parabola through s = 0.95, 1.0, 1.05 (entries 1, 2, 3).
bottom_s = 1.0 + 0.05 * (stretch_E[1] - stretch_E[3]) / (2.0 * (stretch_E[1] - 2.0 * stretch_E[2] + stretch_E[3]))
r_bottom_angstrom = r_water_bohr * bottom_s * BOHR_ANGSTROM
r_stored_angstrom = r_water_bohr * BOHR_ANGSTROM
show r_stored_angstrom
show r_bottom_angstrom

figure("Water's RHF/STO-3G energy along the symmetric stretch", "O-H distance (angstrom)", "energy (hartree)")
plot(stretch_r, stretch_E, "lib/hf")
scatter([r_stored_angstrom], [E_water], "the stored geometry, with both integral methods cross-checked")

test "the energy is PySCF's -74.9630631297292 within 1e-9, with both integral methods cross-checked" {
    assert_near(E_water, -74.9630631297292, 1.0e-9)
    assert_near(eri_families_swept, 2.0, 0.0)
    assert_near(mcmurchie_davidson_and_head_gordon_pople_agree_to_1e_12, 1.0, 0.0)
    assert_lt(eri_report[SW_REP_WORST], 1.0e-12)
    assert_near(water_result.converged, 1.0, 0.0)
}

test "every point of the stretch curve is PySCF's energy at that geometry within 1e-9" {
    for k to len(STRETCH) {
        assert_near(stretch_E[k], STRETCH_PYSCF[k], 1.0e-9)
    }
}

test "the parabola's bottom is within 5e-4 angstrom of PySCF's minimum along the stretch, 0.98704" {
    # 0.9867672575076872: the same parabola through PySCF's three energies
    assert_near(r_bottom_angstrom, 0.9867672575076872, 1.0e-6)
    assert_near(r_bottom_angstrom, 0.9870436921838125, 5.0e-4)
}

test "water in STO-3G is 3 atoms, 5 shells and 15 primitives, 7 basis functions and 406 distinct integrals" {
    assert_near(len(water.atoms), 3, 0)
    assert_near(len(water.shells), 5, 0)
    assert_near(len(water.prims), 15, 0)
    assert_near(len(S_water), 7, 0)
    assert_near(len(G_water), 406, 0)
}

test "the parabola's bottom is 3 percent longer than the stored O-H bond" {
    # 0.987 against 0.958 angstrom; the tolerance is half a percent, half the last stated digit
    assert_near(r_bottom_angstrom / r_stored_angstrom - 1.0, 0.03, 0.005)
}

###
## The density, iteration by iteration

The figure below starts again from the core Hamiltonian, the density of the
electrons with no repulsion between them, and takes plain Roothaan steps:
build $F$ from the density, solve $FC = SC\varepsilon$, fill the five lowest
orbitals, repeat, with no DIIS. Each frame is the electron density
$\rho(\mathbf r) = \sum_{\mu\nu} D_{\mu\nu}\,\phi_\mu(\mathbf r)\,\phi_\nu(\mathbf r)$
in the plane of the molecule, drawn as $\log_{10}\rho$ in bohr$^{-3}$, and
the second figure is the energy of each frame's density. The steps end on
the same energy as the accelerated run above.
###

# the plane of the molecule is x = 0; the picture is a square around it, in bohr
PLANE_N = 40
PLANE_Y = 3.4
PLANE_Z_LO = -2.9
# densities below this are drawn as this, so the log stays finite
RHO_FLOOR = 1.0e-4
# plain steps from the core guess; the energy change after the last is below DENSITY_STEPS_TOL
DENSITY_STEPS = 24
DENSITY_STEPS_TOL = 1.0e-9
# frames drawn: the first steps, where the density moves
DENSITY_FRAMES = 6

#| The value of every basis function of `mol` at the point (x, y, z), in
#| bohr. s and p shells only, in PySCF's order (p as x, y, z).
#@ 629b0fde
def ao_values(mol: Molecule, cn: Arr, x, y, z) {
    vals = zeros(len(S_water))
    for sh to len(mol.shells) {
        at = mol.shells[sh, SH_ATOM]
        dx = x - mol.atoms[at, AT_X]
        dy = y - mol.atoms[at, AT_Y]
        dz = z - mol.atoms[at, AT_Z]
        r2 = dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz
        radial = 0.0
        for p to mol.shells[sh, SH_NPRIM] {
            q = mol.shells[sh, SH_P0] + p
            radial = radial + cn[q] * exp(-mol.prims[q, PR_EXP] * r2)
        }
        c0 = mol.shells[sh, SH_CART0]
        l = mol.shells[sh, SH_L]
        if l == 0 {
            vals[c0] = radial
        }
        else if l == 1 {
            vals[c0] = dx * radial
            vals[c0 + 1] = dy * radial
            vals[c0 + 2] = dz * radial
        }
        else {
            stop("ao_values: s and p shells only")
        }
    }
    return vals
}

#| The overlap of two s shells, by the Gaussian product theorem: an
#| integral lib/hf computes its own way, so comparing the two checks that
#| ao_values reads the tables and the contracted coefficients `cn` as lib/hf does.
#@ 7cf99eef
def ss_overlap(mol: Molecule, cn: Arr, sa, sb) {
    ta = mol.shells[sa, SH_ATOM]
    tb = mol.shells[sb, SH_ATOM]
    r2 = 0.0
    for d to 3 {
        g = mol.atoms[ta, AT_X + d] - mol.atoms[tb, AT_X + d]
        r2 = r2 + g * g
    }
    acc = 0.0
    for i to mol.shells[sa, SH_NPRIM] {
        for j to mol.shells[sb, SH_NPRIM] {
            qi = mol.shells[sa, SH_P0] + i
            qj = mol.shells[sb, SH_P0] + j
            ai = mol.prims[qi, PR_EXP]
            aj = mol.prims[qj, PR_EXP]
            acc = acc + cn[qi] * cn[qj] * pow(pi / (ai + aj), 1.5) * exp(-ai * aj * r2 / (ai + aj))
        }
    }
    return acc
}

#| log10 of the electron density of D on the picture's grid, row 0 at the bottom.
#@ b337ae7b
def density_plane(mol: Molecule, cn: Arr, D: Arr) {
    img = zeros(PLANE_N, PLANE_N)
    side = 2.0 * PLANE_Y
    for r to PLANE_N {
        for c to PLANE_N {
            y = -PLANE_Y + (c + 0.5) * side / PLANE_N
            z = PLANE_Z_LO + (r + 0.5) * side / PLANE_N
            phi = ao_values(mol, cn, 0.0, y, z)
            rho = sum(phi * (D @ phi))
            # two decimals of the log are plenty for a picture and keep the figure data small
            img[r, c] = round(100.0 * log(max(rho, RHO_FLOOR)) / log(10.0)) / 100.0
        }
    }
    return img
}

water_cn = bas_contract(water.shells, water.prims)
water_setup = hf_setup_of(water, H_water, S_water, G_water, scf_defaults())
nao = len(S_water)
step_from_zero = hf_step(water_setup, zeros(nao, nao), zeros(nao, nao))
D_step = step_from_zero.density
step_energy = zeros(DENSITY_STEPS)
step_frames = zeros(DENSITY_FRAMES, PLANE_N, PLANE_N)
for k to DENSITY_STEPS {
    if k < DENSITY_FRAMES {
        step_frames[k, :, :] = density_plane(water, water_cn, D_step)
    }
    stepped = hf_step(water_setup, 0.5 * D_step, 0.5 * D_step)
    step_energy[k] = stepped.energy
    D_step = stepped.density
}
steps_final_energy = step_energy[DENSITY_STEPS - 1]
steps_last_change = abs(step_energy[DENSITY_STEPS - 1] - step_energy[DENSITY_STEPS - 2])
show steps_final_energy
# shells 0 and 1 are oxygen's 1s and 2s, 3 and 4 the hydrogens' 1s; basis functions 0, 1, 5 and 6
ss_gap = max([abs(ss_overlap(water, water_cn, 0, 3) - S_water[0, 5]), abs(ss_overlap(water, water_cn, 1, 3) - S_water[1, 5]), abs(ss_overlap(water, water_cn, 3, 4) - S_water[5, 6])])
show ss_gap

figure("Water's electron density, one plain Roothaan step per frame", "y (bohr)", "z (bohr)", -PLANE_Y, PLANE_Y, PLANE_Z_LO, PLANE_Z_LO + 2.0 * PLANE_Y)
origin("lower")
label("O", "O", water.atoms[0, AT_Y], water.atoms[0, AT_Z])
label("H1", "H", water.atoms[1, AT_Y], water.atoms[1, AT_Z])
label("H2", "H", water.atoms[2, AT_Y], water.atoms[2, AT_Z])
for k to DENSITY_FRAMES {
    plot2d(slab(step_frames, k), "log10 of the density (bohr^-3)")
}
figure("The energy of each step's density", "step", "energy (hartree)")
plot(linspace(1.0, DENSITY_STEPS, DENSITY_STEPS), step_energy, "plain Roothaan steps from the core guess")
hline("the accelerated run", E_water)

test "the basis functions on the grid are the ones lib/hf integrates: three of their overlaps are S's within 1e-12" {
    assert_lt(ss_gap, 1.0e-12)
}
test "the plain steps end on the accelerated run's energy within 1e-9" {
    assert_lt(steps_last_change, DENSITY_STEPS_TOL)
    assert_near(steps_final_energy, E_water, 1.0e-9)
}

functions.name: row_length
functions.what: How many entries each row of a block has.

functions.name: row_norms
functions.what: The Euclidean norm of each row of `a`: one number per vector in a block.

functions.name: divide_rows
functions.what: Divide each row of `a` by its entry in `norms`, in place. A zero row stays zero instead of becoming a row of NaN.

functions.name: stacked
functions.what: The rows of `top` followed by the rows of `bottom`, as one block.

functions.name: rayleigh_quotients
functions.what: The Rayleigh quotient of each row, $\lambda_b = x_b^H H x_b$ for a unit row $x_b$: the best estimate of an eigenvalue that the vector alone can give.

functions.name: residuals
functions.what: The residual of each row, $r_b = H x_b - \lambda_b x_b$. It is zero exactly when $x_b$ is an eigenvector, and its norm bounds the distance from $\lambda_b$ to the nearest eigenvalue.

functions.name: largest_of_first
functions.what: The largest of the first `count` entries of `a` (all of them if there are fewer).

functions.name: no_preconditioner
functions.what: The identity preconditioner, for an operator with nothing better.

functions.name: orthonormalizer
functions.what: A matrix `m` whose rows make the rows of `m @ s` orthonormal and span what the rows of `s` span, minus the directions `s` barely has.

functions.name: lowest_ritz_coefficients
functions.what: Rayleigh-Ritz: of all unit vectors in the span of the orthonormal rows of `s`, the `nb` with the lowest Rayleigh quotients, as coefficients: row b of the result times `s` is the b-th lowest Ritz vector.

functions.name: search_directions
functions.what: The search directions for one step: each row's residual, preconditioned. A row whose residual is under `lock` has converged and offers none (its row stays zero, and `orthonormalizer` drops it). This is soft locking: the row still takes part in Rayleigh-Ritz, so it keeps improving from the others' directions, but no work is spent pushing it further.

functions.name: lobpcg_start
functions.what: A LOBPCG state for the starting rows of `x`: orthonormalized, rotated into Ritz vectors of their own span, and with no previous step yet.

functions.name: lobpcg_step
functions.what: One LOBPCG step on `state`, in place. Returns the largest residual norm among the lowest `nconv` rows before the step; when that is already under `tol` the state is left alone. `step` counts from 0; step 0 has no previous step p to search along.

functions.name: lobpcg
functions.what: The lowest eigenpairs of the Hermitian operator `apply_h`, starting from the rows of `vectors`, which come back holding the eigenvectors; `values` gets the eigenvalues. At most `max_steps` steps; stops once the lowest `nconv` rows have residual norms under `tol`, and returns the largest of those.

functions.name: apply_laplacian_1d
functions.what: The second-difference matrix on n points with zero ends: 2 on the diagonal and -1 beside it, applied to each row. Its eigenvalues are known exactly: $2 - 2\cos(k\pi / (n + 1))$, k = 1 .. n.

functions.name: apply_laplacian_2d
functions.what: The five-point Laplacian on an m by m grid with zero edges, each row of `x` being a grid stored row after row. Its eigenvalues are sums of two of the 1-D ones.

functions.name: unstructured_matrix
functions.what: A real symmetric n by n matrix with no structure to exploit: 1 .. n down the diagonal, so the spectrum is spread out, and $\sin((i+1)(j+1))$ off it.

functions.name: apply_unstructured
functions.what: `unstructured_matrix` applied to each row, as a complex operator.

functions.name: random_rows
functions.what: nb random starting rows of length n.

functions.name: worst_eigen_residual
functions.what: The largest residual norm $|H x_b - \lambda_b x_b|$ among the first `count` rows, with H applied afresh: a check on the solver that does not take its word for H x.

functions.name: kinetic_real
functions.what: $-\frac12 \nabla^2 \psi$ on the grid, for each row of a real block: the five-point stencil $(4\psi_{ij} - \psi_{i\pm1,j} - \psi_{i,j\pm1}) / 2h^2$. `roll` along the row brings each point's neighbor to it; the masks zero the neighbors that fall outside the box.

functions.name: apply_box
functions.what: The Hamiltonian of a particle in a box, applied to each row of `x`. It is real, so it acts on the real and imaginary parts separately.

functions.name: grid_level
functions.what: The exact eigenvalue of the grid Hamiltonian for the mode with j and k half-waves: a sum of two 1-D second-difference eigenvalues.

functions.name: box_level
functions.what: The level of the same mode in the continuous box, $\pi^2 (j^2 + k^2) / 2$.

functions.name: converge
functions.what: Run LOBPCG a step at a time from the rows of `start`, recording each wanted state's residual norm (log10) and eigenvalue error (log10) per step in `residual_log` and `error_log`. With `use_previous_step` false every step is taken as step 0, which never searches along p: that is block steepest descent. Returns the number of steps taken to converge, or `max_steps`.

functions.name: history
functions.what: Row `s` of a per-step log, its first `n` entries.

functions.name: worst_per_step
functions.what: The largest entry of each column of a per-step log, its first `n` columns: the worst of the wanted states at each step.

functions.name: state_picture
functions.what: State `s` as an M by M picture: row i, column j is the grid point (i, j).
